project.name: Arij
project.description: A local, AI-first project orchestrator that provides a web interface for managing multi-project workflows with Claude Code as the execution engine. It covers the full project lifecycle: ideation, specification, kanban-based planning, automated code generation via Claude Code CLI, real-time agent monitoring, and release management.
project.spec:
# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

Arij is a local-first web app that lets you plan, organize, and build software projects using AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code). You describe features as epics; Arij orchestrates the agents, manages git branches and worktrees, runs reviews, and merges the result. Everything runs on your machine — no cloud, no account, no telemetry.

---

## 1. Objectives of this iteration

Today a project can only be attached to a directory that **already exists on disk** (`app/projects/new/page.tsx` and `app/projects/import/page.tsx` both ask for a filesystem path, validated by `lib/validation/path.ts`, which requires an existing directory). Arij never clones anything.

This iteration adds a third entry point: **import a project directly from a GitHub URL**. Arij clones the repository into an app-managed workspace directory and then works from that clone exactly as it would from a user-supplied local repo.

Goals:

1. Paste `https://github.com/owner/repo` (or `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, or `owner/repo`) in the Import flow and get a fully set-up Arij project.
2. Clone into a predictable, app-managed root — `<arij>/projects/` by default, overridable in Settings.
3. Support private repositories using the GitHub PAT already stored in the `settings` table (`github_pat`), **without ever persisting the token to disk**.
4. Reuse the entire existing import pipeline unchanged: Claude analysis, `arji.json` short-circuit, epic/story creation, `arji.json` export.
5. Auto-populate `githubOwnerRepo` so push / PR / release / issue-sync features work immediately, with no manual "Connect GitHub" step.

## 2. Constraints

- **Migrations are hand-written.** `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run: the `meta/*_snapshot.json` files stop at 0013 while the journal reaches 0026, so generate would produce a wrong diff. The new migration is authored by hand as `0027_project_clone_source.sql` and appended to `meta/_journal.json` at `idx: 26`.
- **Full clones only.** Arij creates worktrees, branches, merges and tags (`lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/git/release.ts`). A shallow clone (`--depth`) would break `worktree add` from `main` and merge-base computation. No `--depth`, no `--single-branch`.
- **No new git library.** `simple-git@^3.30` is the only git dependency; `@octokit/rest@^22` is the only GitHub API client. The `gh` CLI is not used anywhere and must not be introduced.
- **No new job infrastructure.** The existing import already blocks on a multi-minute `POST /api/projects/import` call. Clone follows the same synchronous request/response shape; only the UI gains a distinct progress step.
- **Credentials live in SQLite, not env.** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is documented in the README but unused in code; the real source is `getGitHubTokenFromSettings()` in `lib/github/client.ts`.

## 3. Technical stack

Unchanged: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui, SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle, `simple-git`, `@octokit/rest`, nanoid IDs, Vitest + Playwright.

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Workspace layout

```
<arij>/
  data/                  # DB, session logs, uploads (gitignored)
  projects/              # NEW — app-managed clone root (gitignored)
    <owner>-<repo>/      # the clone; becomes projects.git_repo_path
    .arij-worktrees/     # created automatically by createWorktree()
```

`lib/git/manager.ts:37` places worktrees at `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")`. With a clone at `projects/<owner>-<repo>`, worktrees land in `projects/.arij-worktrees` — no change to the worktree code is required, but `/projects` must be added to `.gitignore` so Arij's own repo stays clean when dogfooding.

The root is resolved by a new `lib/projects/workspace.ts`, reading the `projects_root` settings key with a `<cwd>/projects` default. Following the established convention (`lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts`, `lib/night/constants.ts`), the key name, default and parser live in a client-safe `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` that does not import `db`.

### 4.2 Request flow

```
User pastes GitHub URL
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/clone            <-- NEW
  parse URL -> { owner, repo }
  resolve dest = <projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>
  if dest exists && origin matches  -> reuse (fetch only)
  else git clone (token via -c http.extraHeader)
  -> { path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/import           <-- EXISTING, unchanged
  validatePath(path) -> arji.json short-circuit OR Claude analysis
  -> { preview, path, fromExistingFile }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects                  <-- EXISTING, + githubOwnerRepo/clone metadata
PATCH /api/projects/:id, epics, user-stories, sync export
```

Splitting clone from analysis keeps `POST /api/projects/import` untouched and gives the UI two honest progress steps ("Cloning…" then "Analyzing…") instead of one opaque spinner.

### 4.3 URL parsing

`lib/git/remote.ts` already exports `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`, covering `git@github.com:`, `ssh://`, `https://`, `git://`. A new `parseGitHubRepoInput()` wraps it and additionally accepts the shorthand `owner/repo` and browser URLs carrying a suffix (`/tree/main`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme`). Owner and repo are then re-validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and rejected if either is `.` or `..`, so a crafted URL can never escape the clone root.

### 4.4 Credential handling

The clone runs as:

```
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:PAT)>" \
    clone --no-tags=false <clean-https-url> <dest>
```

Because the header is passed with `-c` it is never written to `.git/config`; `origin` keeps the clean URL, so subsequent `fetch`/`pull`/`push` behave exactly like a hand-made clone and no secret is stored on disk. Any error string returned to the client is passed through a redaction helper that strips `Basic <...>` and `://user:pass@` fragments before it reaches the UI or `git_sync_log`. Public repositories clone with no token at all.

### 4.5 Data model

`projects` gains three nullable columns (migration `0027`):

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clone_source` | `"github"` when Arij created the directory, `NULL` for user-supplied paths |
| `git_remote_url` | the clean clone URL, for display and re-clone |
| `default_branch` | branch reported by the clone, used instead of the `main`/`master` guess |

`clone_source` is the ownership flag: only directories Arij created may be offered for deletion when a project is deleted. Existing rows keep `NULL` and behave exactly as today.

### 4.6 Observability

Each clone writes a `git_sync_log` row with `operation = "clone"` (the column is free-form text, so no schema change is needed) recording the owner/repo, destination, duration, whether the clone was reused, and the redacted error on failure.

## 5. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Clone root defaults to `<cwd>/projects`, configurable via `projects_root` | Matches the user's request; the setting keeps users who store code elsewhere in control. |
| Destination is `<owner>-<repo>` | Deterministic and collision-free across owners; makes re-import idempotent. |
| Existing directory with a matching `origin` is reused (fetch, no re-clone) | Same idempotent posture as `createWorktree()`; re-running an import is cheap and safe. Mismatched remote returns 409 rather than silently overwriting. |
| Token injected via `-c http.extraHeader`, not embedded in the remote URL | A token baked into `origin` would persist in `.git/config` forever and leak through every diff/log surface. |
| Clone is a separate endpoint, not a flag on `/api/projects/import` | Keeps the analysis route untouched, gives real progress steps, and makes clone independently testable. |
| No shallow clone | Worktrees, merges and tags need full history. |
| Partial clone on failure is deleted | Avoids a half-clone being reused later as a "matching" repo. |

## 6. Out of scope

Non-GitHub hosts (GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted), SSH-key-based clones of private repos, background/queued cloning with cancellation, and monorepo sub-directory imports. The parsing layer is written so a second host can be added later without touching the clone service.

epics.title: Création directe d'epic depuis le bouton New et paste d'image dans la création de bug
epics.description:
## Contexte

Aujourd'hui la création d'une epic passe obligatoirement par le chat unifié (panneau gauche) : l'utilisateur discute avec l'agent, puis demande "Generate the final epic with user stories" et l'agent renvoie un bloc JSON qui est parsé pour créer l'epic et ses user stories. Ce parcours est excellent pour brainstormer, mais il est lourd quand l'utilisateur sait déjà exactement ce qu'il veut créer : il doit attendre une réponse d'agent (avec les aléas de parsing JSON, les réponses vides, les latences) pour obtenir un ticket qu'il aurait pu écrire lui-même en quinze secondes.

Par ailleurs, la création de bug accepte du texte mais pas d'image, alors que le chat supporte déjà l'upload et le paste d'images depuis le presse-papier. Or un bug se décrit très souvent par une capture d'écran : c'est le cas d'usage le plus naturel pour un attachement visuel, et c'est justement là qu'il manque.

## Objectifs

1. Le bouton New propose deux chemins explicites : création manuelle d'epic (formulaire direct, aucun agent impliqué) ou création via le chat (parcours actuel, inchangé).
2. Le formulaire de création manuelle permet de saisir titre, description, et d'ajouter des user stories à la volée (titre, description, critères d'acceptation), avec au minimum zéro user story autorisée.
3. La modale de création de bug accepte les images : bouton d'upload, drag & drop, et surtout Ctrl/Cmd+V depuis le presse-papier, en réutilisant le pipeline d'upload déjà en place pour le chat.
4. Les images attachées à un bug sont persistées, affichées en miniature dans le détail du ticket, et transmises à l'agent lorsqu'il est dispatché sur le bug (même mécanisme que les images de chat).

## Plan d'implémentation

### 1. Point d'entrée « New » (UI)

- Transformer le bouton New existant en menu déroulant (`DropdownMenu` shadcn/ui) avec deux entrées : *New Epic* et *New Bug* si ce n'est pas déjà le cas, plus un sous-choix pour l'epic : *Créer manuellement* / *Créer via le chat*.
- L'entrée « via le chat » conserve strictement le comportement actuel (ouverture du panneau de chat unifié en mode création d'epic).
- L'entrée « manuellement » ouvre une nouvelle modale `CreateEpicDialog`.
- Aucune régression sur le parcours chat : le composant de chat n'est pas modifié.

### 2. Modale `CreateEpicDialog`

- Nouveau composant `components/epics/create-epic-dialog.tsx` construit sur `Dialog` + `Form` (shadcn/ui) et sur les mêmes primitives que les modales existantes.
- Champs : `title` (requis, non vide, trim), `description` (textarea markdown, optionnel).
- Section « User stories » : liste dynamique de blocs repliables, chacun avec `title`, `description`, `acceptanceCriteria` (textarea markdown, checklist). Boutons *Ajouter une user story* et *Supprimer*. Réordonnancement non requis dans cette itération.
- Validation côté client avant submit : titre d'epic requis ; toute user story ajoutée doit avoir un titre non vide.
- État de soumission : bouton désactivé + spinner, gestion d'erreur affichée en ligne, pas de fermeture de modale tant que la requête n'a pas réussi.

### 3. Backend — création directe

- Réutiliser les routes existantes `POST /api/epics` et `POST /api/user-stories` plutôt que d'inventer un nouvel endpoint, en enchaînant les appels côté client, OU exposer `POST /api/epics` avec un tableau `userStories` optionnel créé en transaction si le contrat actuel s'y prête. Trancher au moment de l'implémentation après lecture des routes ; la solution transactionnelle est préférée pour éviter les epics orphelines en cas d'échec partiel.
- L'epic créée manuellement doit atterrir dans la même colonne kanban par défaut et avec le même tri (date de création) que les epics issues du chat — aucun champ de statut spécial.
- Les IDs sont générés via `nanoid` (`lib/utils/nanoid.ts`) comme partout ailleurs.

### 4. Images dans la création de bug

- Localiser le pipeline d'upload d'images du chat (composant d'input de chat + route d'upload sous `app/api/`, stockage dans `data/uploads`) et l'extraire dans un hook/composant réutilisable si ce n'est pas déjà fait (ex. `hooks/use-image-paste.ts` + `components/shared/image-attachments.tsx`).
- Brancher ce composant dans la modale de création de bug : bouton *Joindre une image*, zone de drop, et handler `onPaste` sur le champ de description capturant `event.clipboardData.files`.
- Miniatures avec suppression individuelle avant soumission ; contrôle du type MIME (image/*) et d'une taille max cohérente avec la limite déjà appliquée au chat.
- Persistance : rattacher les images au ticket bug via le même modèle que les pièces jointes de chat (table/colonne existante réutilisée si possible, sinon colonne JSON `attachments` sur le ticket, migration écrite à la main — `npx drizzle-kit generate` est interdit sur ce dépôt).
- Affichage : miniatures cliquables dans le détail du ticket bug, ouverture en grand.
- Dispatch agent : lorsque le bug est envoyé à un agent, les chemins d'images sont injectés dans le prompt comme pour le chat, afin que l'agent puisse effectivement les lire.

### 5. Tests

- Tests unitaires (Vitest) sur la validation du formulaire d'epic et sur le helper de normalisation des pièces jointes.
- Test E2E (Playwright) : ouvrir New → Epic manuelle → remplir titre + 2 user stories → vérifier l'apparition de la carte dans le kanban et des user stories dans le détail.
- Test E2E : ouvrir New → Bug → coller une image → soumettre → vérifier la miniature dans le détail du ticket.

## Hors périmètre

Réordonnancement drag & drop des user stories dans le formulaire, édition en masse, templates d'epic, upload de fichiers non-image (PDF, logs) sur les bugs, et conversion automatique d'une epic manuelle en discussion de chat.

user_stories.title: As a user, I want the New button to offer both manual epic creation and chat-based creation so that I can choose the fastest path for what I already know
user_stories.description: Le bouton New devient un menu explicite qui laisse le choix entre créer une epic à la main (formulaire) et la créer via le chat unifié (parcours actuel). L'objectif est de ne plus imposer un aller-retour agent quand l'utilisateur sait déjà ce qu'il veut écrire, tout en préservant intégralement le parcours de brainstorming existant.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Le bouton New ouvre un menu déroulant listant au minimum « Nouvelle epic (manuelle) », « Nouvelle epic (via le chat) » et « Nouveau bug »
- [ ] « Via le chat » ouvre le panneau de chat unifié en mode création d'epic, avec exactement le comportement actuel (aucune régression)
- [ ] « Manuelle » ouvre la modale de création directe sans déclencher aucun appel agent
- [ ] Le menu est accessible au clavier (flèches, Entrée, Échap) et fonctionne en dark mode
- [ ] Aucun appel réseau vers un provider d'agent n'est émis lors du choix « Manuelle »

user_stories.title: As a user, I want a direct epic creation form with title, description and inline user stories so that I can create a complete ticket without waiting for an agent
user_stories.description: Nouvelle modale CreateEpicDialog permettant de saisir le titre et la description d'une epic, et d'ajouter dynamiquement autant de user stories que souhaité (titre, description, critères d'acceptation en markdown). Zéro user story est un cas valide.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] La modale expose un champ titre requis et une description markdown optionnelle
- [ ] Un bouton « Ajouter une user story » ajoute un bloc avec titre, description et critères d'acceptation
- [ ] Chaque user story peut être supprimée individuellement avant soumission
- [ ] Une epic sans aucune user story peut être créée
- [ ] Le submit est bloqué si le titre de l'epic est vide ou si une user story ajoutée n'a pas de titre, avec un message d'erreur en ligne
- [ ] Pendant la soumission le bouton est désactivé et un indicateur de chargement est affiché

user_stories.title: As a user, I want the manually created epic to be persisted atomically with its user stories so that I never end up with an orphan epic
user_stories.description: Câblage backend de la création directe : l'epic et ses user stories sont écrites en base de façon cohérente, en réutilisant les routes et conventions existantes (nanoid pour les IDs, forme de réponse { data } / { error }). En cas d'échec partiel, rien n'est persisté.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] L'epic et ses user stories sont créées dans une seule opération cohérente (transaction) ou, à défaut, un échec sur les user stories supprime l'epic créée
- [ ] Les IDs sont générés via lib/utils/nanoid.ts
- [ ] La réponse API respecte la forme { data } en succès et { error } en échec
- [ ] L'epic apparaît immédiatement dans le kanban après création, dans la colonne par défaut et au bon rang selon le tri par date de création
- [ ] Aucune modification du parcours de création via le chat n'est nécessaire côté backend

user_stories.title: As a user, I want to paste a screenshot directly into the bug creation modal so that I can report a visual defect without saving a file first
user_stories.description: La modale de création de bug accepte les images via Ctrl/Cmd+V depuis le presse-papier, via un bouton d'upload et via drag & drop, en réutilisant le pipeline d'upload déjà utilisé par le chat plutôt qu'en le dupliquant.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Ctrl/Cmd+V dans la modale de bug attache l'image présente dans le presse-papier
- [ ] Un bouton « Joindre une image » et le drag & drop permettent le même résultat
- [ ] Les fichiers non-image sont refusés avec un message clair, de même que les fichiers dépassant la limite de taille appliquée au chat
- [ ] Les images attachées s'affichent en miniature dans la modale et peuvent être retirées une par une avant soumission
- [ ] Le code d'upload est mutualisé avec celui du chat (hook ou composant partagé), sans duplication de la logique de transfert

user_stories.title: As a user, I want bug attachments to be stored and visible in the ticket detail so that the screenshot stays available after creation
user_stories.description: Persistance et restitution des images attachées à un bug : stockage aligné sur celui des images de chat, affichage en miniatures cliquables dans le détail du ticket, ouverture en grand format.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Les images sont persistées et rattachées au ticket bug lors de la création
- [ ] Le détail du ticket affiche les miniatures des images attachées
- [ ] Un clic sur une miniature ouvre l'image en grand
- [ ] Toute évolution de schéma est faite via une migration SQL écrite à la main et ajoutée au journal, sans exécuter npx drizzle-kit generate
- [ ] Les tickets bug existants sans image continuent de s'afficher normalement

user_stories.title: As a developer agent, I want the bug screenshots to be passed in my prompt so that I can actually diagnose the reported visual issue
user_stories.description: Lorsqu'un bug avec images est envoyé à un agent (Send-to-Dev, Create And Fix, review), les chemins des images attachées sont injectés dans le prompt selon le même mécanisme que les images du chat, afin que l'agent puisse les lire.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Le prompt envoyé à l'agent référence les chemins locaux des images attachées au bug
- [ ] Le mécanisme d'injection réutilise celui déjà en place pour les images de chat
- [ ] Un bug sans image produit un prompt inchangé par rapport à aujourd'hui
- [ ] Le comportement est identique quel que soit le provider CLI sélectionné pour l'agent

user_stories.title: As a maintainer, I want automated coverage of both new flows so that direct creation and image paste do not silently regress
user_stories.description: Tests unitaires Vitest sur la validation du formulaire et la normalisation des pièces jointes, plus deux scénarios Playwright couvrant la création manuelle d'epic avec user stories et la création d'un bug avec image collée.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Test unitaire couvrant le refus d'un titre d'epic vide et d'une user story sans titre
- [ ] Test unitaire couvrant le filtrage des fichiers non-image et hors limite de taille
- [ ] Test E2E : New → epic manuelle avec 2 user stories → carte visible dans le kanban et user stories visibles dans le détail
- [ ] Test E2E : New → bug → image collée → miniature visible dans le détail du ticket après création
- [ ] La suite de tests passe intégralement en local

epics.title: La modal des review est trop petite, teubé
Socle du workspace de clones (répertoire `projects/` + schéma)
epics.description: Introduce the app-managed clone root and the project metadata needed to track Arij-owned clones. Adds `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` (client-safe: settings key `projects_root`, default `<cwd>/projects`, parser — same pattern as `lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts`) and `lib/projects/workspace.ts` (server-side: `resolveProjectsRoot()`, `ensureProjectsRoot()`, `cloneDestinationFor(owner, repo)`, `assertInsideRoot(dest)`). Adds the hand-written migration `0027_project_clone_source.sql` with `clone_source`, `git_remote_url`, `default_branch` on `projects`, updates `lib/db/schema.ts`, and appends `idx: 26` to `meta/_journal.json`. Adds `/projects` to `.gitignore`. Exposes the root in the Settings page next to the existing GitHub PAT section. CRITICAL: do not run `npx drizzle-kit generate` — snapshots stop at 0013 while the journal is at 0026, so generate emits a wrong diff; write the SQL by hand.

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want a single helper that resolves the clone root so that every clone lands in a predictable, configurable directory
user_stories.description: Create `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` with `PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY = "projects_root"`, `DEFAULT_PROJECTS_DIRNAME = "projects"` and a `parseProjectsRoot(value)` helper, importable from client components without pulling in `db`. Create `lib/projects/workspace.ts` that reads the settings row, falls back to `path.join(process.cwd(), "projects")`, and exposes `ensureProjectsRoot()` (mkdir recursive) and `cloneDestinationFor(owner, repo)`.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` exports the key, the default and a parser, and imports nothing from `@/lib/db`
- [ ] `resolveProjectsRoot()` returns the `projects_root` settings value when set, `<cwd>/projects` otherwise
- [ ] A configured relative root is resolved against `process.cwd()` and returned absolute
- [ ] `cloneDestinationFor("Orolol", "arij")` returns `<root>/Orolol-arij`
- [ ] `assertInsideRoot()` throws for any destination that resolves outside the root
- [ ] `ensureProjectsRoot()` creates the directory recursively and is a no-op when it already exists
- [ ] Unit tests cover default, override, relative-root and escape-attempt cases

user_stories.title: As Arij, I want to record how a project's directory came to exist so that I only ever clean up directories I created
user_stories.description: Add `clone_source` (text, nullable — `"github"` or NULL), `git_remote_url` (text, nullable) and `default_branch` (text, nullable) to the `projects` table via a hand-written migration, and mirror them in `lib/db/schema.ts`.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `lib/db/migrations/0027_project_clone_source.sql` contains three `ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN` statements
- [ ] `meta/_journal.json` gains an entry with `idx: 26`, `tag: "0027_project_clone_source"`
- [ ] `npx drizzle-kit generate` is NOT run; snapshots are untouched
- [ ] `projects` in `lib/db/schema.ts` declares `cloneSource`, `gitRemoteUrl`, `defaultBranch`
- [ ] Existing project rows keep `NULL` in all three columns and behave exactly as before
- [ ] `ensureDbReady()` applies the migration cleanly on an existing dev database

user_stories.title: As a user, I want to choose where Arij clones repositories so that my code lives where I expect it
user_stories.description: Add a "Projects directory" field to `app/settings/page.tsx`, following the existing per-section `saving*` / `*Message` state pattern. It persists through `PATCH /api/settings` under `projects_root` and shows the effective default as placeholder when empty.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The Settings page shows a "Projects directory" input with the resolved default as placeholder
- [ ] Saving persists `projects_root` and shows the section's success message
- [ ] `PATCH /api/settings` rejects a non-string value for `projects_root` with 400
- [ ] A blank value clears the override and restores the default
- [ ] Changing the root does not move or break existing projects

user_stories.title: As a maintainer, I want cloned repositories excluded from Arij's own git history so that dogfooding never pollutes the repo
user_stories.description: Add `/projects` to the root `.gitignore`. Confirm that worktrees created for cloned projects land in `projects/.arij-worktrees` (from `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")` at `lib/git/manager.ts:37`) and are therefore covered by the same rule.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `.gitignore` contains `/projects`
- [ ] `git status` is clean after cloning a repository into the default root
- [ ] `git status` is clean after building an epic on a cloned project (worktree in `projects/.arij-worktrees`)
- [ ] `git check-ignore -v projects/owner-repo` confirms the rule

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
## Socle du workspace de clones — implémenté ✅

Commit `bcbe9c2`. Suite complète verte : **2444 tests / 254 fichiers**, `tsc --noEmit` propre, aucun lint nouveau.

### US1 — Helper de résolution de la racine
- `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` (client-safe) : `PROJECTS_ROOT_SETTING_KEY`, `DEFAULT_PROJECTS_DIRNAME`, `parseProjectsRoot()`. N'importe **ni** `@/lib/db` **ni** `node:*` (assertion dans les tests).
- `lib/projects/workspace.ts` : `resolveProjectsRoot()`, `defaultProjectsRoot()`, `ensureProjectsRoot()`, `cloneDestinationFor()`, `assertInsideRoot()`.
- Une racine relative est résolue contre `process.cwd()` et renvoyée absolue ; `cloneDestinationFor("Orolol", "arij")` → `<root>/Orolol-arij` ; owner/repo validés par `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` avec rejet de `.`/`..`, puis destination re-vérifiée contre la racine.
- 22 tests (`__tests__/projects-workspace.test.ts`) : défaut, override, racine relative, tentatives d'évasion, `mkdir` idempotent.

### US2 — Provenance du répertoire
- `0027_project_clone_source.sql` : trois `ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN` (`clone_source`, `git_remote_url`, `default_branch`), journal `idx: 26`.

## Pi + Oh My Pi ajoutés aux providers CLI

Commit `46eab87`. Suite complète verte (257 fichiers / 2544 tests), `tsc --noEmit` clean.

### Ce que sont réellement ces deux CLI

- **Pi** = `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, binaire `pi` — harness terminal minimal, headless via `--mode json`.
- **Oh My Pi** = paquet npm `oh-my-pi`, **extension de Pi**, pas un agent autonome : son binaire `oh-my-pi` ne fait que `doctor`/`init`/`version`. L'agent, c'est `pi` avec l'extension chargée (prompt système remplacé par un orchestrateur multi-agents).

Il est donc modélisé comme `pi … -e oh-my-pi`. `-e` résout les sources npm à la demande, donc ça marche que l'utilisateur ait fait `pi install oh-my-pi` ou non (réseau requis au premier run). La disponibilité se réduit à « `pi` est dans le PATH », comme pour Pi.

### Comportement des providers

| | Pi / Oh My Pi |
|---|---|
| Commande | `pi --mode json [--tools …] [--session <ID>] [--model <M>] [-e oh-my-pi] -p <prompt>` |
| plan / analyze | `--tools read,grep,find,ls` (pi n'a pas de système de permissions — la capacité passe par l'allowlist d'outils) |
| code | jeu d'outils par défaut (ajoute write, edit, bash) |
| Résultat | dernier `message_end` assistant — exactement ce que le mode texte de pi imprime — avec repli sur les tours précédents puis sur la sortie brute |
| Resume | `--session <ID>`, id pris dans l'en-tête `{"type":"session","id":…}` du flux |

**Point non évident :** en `--mode json`, pi sort avec le code 0 **même quand le run s'est terminé sur une erreur modèle** (seul son mode texte mappe ça sur exit 1). `handleExit()` déclasse donc le succès en se basant sur le `stopReason` du dernier tour, pas sur le code de sortie. Sans ça, un run raté serait enregistré comme réussi.

### Câblage

`ProviderType`, registre, `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` / `PROVIDER_LABELS` / `PROVIDER_TIERS` (Tier 2), `/api/providers/available`, `useProvidersAvailable`, classification resume. Les deux sont ajoutés **en fin** de `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` pour que la ségrégation reviewer/builder continue de choisir les mêmes alternatives qu'avant.

- `normalizeProvider()` dans `agent-resolution.ts` était une chaîne de 9 `if` à maintenir en phase avec `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` → remplacée par `isAgentProvider()` (idiome déjà utilisé dans `named-agents.ts`).

35 tests unitaires dans `__tests__/pi-providers.test.ts` (args, parsing du flux, extraction du session id, détection d'échec, cycle de spawn complet avec `child_process` mocké).

En plus des tests, j'ai fait tourner les arguments que le provider émet à travers le **vrai parseur de pi** (`dist/cli/args.js` du paquet publié) : aucun flag inconnu, aucun diagnostic, le prompt arrive bien dans `messages`.

**Limite documentée dans le code :** pi ne traite l'argument après `-p` comme prompt que s'il ne commence pas par `-`, et n'offre pas de séparateur `--`. Un prompt commençant par un tiret simple serait avalé comme option inconnue (run avec prompt vide). Inatteignable aujourd'hui — tous les prompts Arij sont composés par template et commencent par un titre — mais c'est noté dans `lib/providers/pi.ts`.

### Hors périmètre

Le chat streaming (`/chat/stream`, `/sessions/resumable`) restreint déjà les providers à claude-code / gemini-cli / codex par une allowlist en dur, antérieure à ce ticket. Je ne l'ai pas élargie : c'est une décision produit séparée. MCP reste limité à claude-code / codex — pi n'a pas de support MCP natif (uniquement via un adaptateur tiers).

## What I found first

The ticket had no user stories, so I researched what these CLIs actually are before writing code. The important discovery:

**Oh My Pi is not an agent CLI.** It's an npm *extension* for Pi — its own `oh-my-pi` binary only does `doctor`/`init`/`version`. The agent is `pi` with the extension loaded, which swaps Pi's system prompt for a multi-agent orchestrator. So it's modelled as `pi … -e oh-my-pi`, not as a separate binary.

**Pi** is `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (binary `pi`), headless via `--mode json`.

`lib/providers/pi.ts` + `lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts` (the latter extends the former, adding `-e oh-my-pi`):

- **Mode mapping** — Pi has no permission system, so capability rides on the tool allowlist: plan/analyze get `--tools read,grep,find,ls`; code keeps the default set.
- **Result** — last assistant `message_end`, which is exactly what Pi's own text mode prints.
- **Resume** — `--session <ID>` from the stream's session header.

One non-obvious thing worth flagging: **in `--mode json`, Pi exits 0 even when the run ended on a model error** — only its text mode maps that to exit 1. `handleExit()` therefore downgrades success based on the final turn's `stopReason`. Without that, failed runs would be recorded as successful.

- `cloneGitHubRepo()` throws `CloneServiceUnavailableError` until epic `drG2ZnRFKHeC` fills in the body.

`POST /api/projects/clone` now calls the service and returns its result (200), mapping `CloneServiceUnavailableError` to 501. This also shrinks the merge surface I flagged earlier: the clone epic replaces **one function body**, not the route.

A raw git failure can echo back the `http.extraHeader` `Authorization: Basic …` value, and the redaction helper from spec §4.4 lands with the clone epic — so until then nothing from the git layer reaches the client. There's a test asserting the 500 body contains neither `Basic` nor `Authorization`.

### 1. Major — PAT is sent when cloning public repositories

- **Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:312](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/lib/git/clone.ts:312)

- **Recommendation:** Clone anonymously first and retry with the PAT only for private/access failures, or determine repository visibility through GitHub. Add a configured-PAT/public-repository test asserting no header is used.

### 2. Major — Reused private clones fetch without PAT or timeout

- **Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:282](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/lib/git/clone.ts:282)
- **Description:** The reuse path calls `fetchGitRemote(dest)` without the stored PAT, non-interactive environment, or abort signal. A private clone created using only Arij’s PAT can therefore fail on re-import or wait indefinitely for credentials.
- **Recommendation:** Execute the fetch with the same command-scoped authorization, non-interactive environment, and configured timeout as clone. Add authenticated-reuse and fetch-timeout tests.

### 3. Major — Reuse can validate one remote and fetch another

- **Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:264](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/lib/git/clone.ts:264)
- **Description:** `detectGitHubRemote()` searches every remote. A matching secondary GitHub remote can approve reuse even when `origin` references a different repository; the code then fetches `origin`. This violates the requirement that the existing clone’s origin match.
- **Recommendation:** Inspect and compare `origin` specifically, then fetch that verified remote. Change the existing secondary-remote test to expect HTTP 409 when origin differs.

### 4. Major — Failed-clone cleanup has a data-loss race

- **Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:222](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC-service-de-clone-git-et-endpoint-post-ap/lib/git/clone.ts:222)

Epic delivered — 3 commits, full suite green (2496 tests / 257 files), `tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint clean on every file I touched.

## What I built

**Story 1 — deletion cleanup.** `DELETE /api/projects/[projectId]?removeDirectory=true`, honoured only when two independent gates both pass: `clone_source = "github"` **and** the path is a strict descendant of the current projects root. A refusal isn't an error — the project is deleted either way and the response reports which gate refused. Removal runs `git worktree prune`, then detaches and deletes the worktrees **git has registered** for that clone (worktrees are named after the branch, not the repo, so guessing directory names would hit the wrong clone), then the clone. The shared `.arij-worktrees` is never removed. Sessions and ephemeral activities are cancelled on every delete, and per-project settings rows are swept — `settings` has no FK to `projects`, so they'd otherwise be inherited by a later project reusing the id.

**Story 2 — resume.** Destination classification decides between three outcomes: healthy clone of the same repo → fetch only, `reused: true`; clone of a *different* repo → 409, never overwritten; debris from an interrupted run (`.git` present, HEAD unborn) → replaced, not reported as a conflict. A valid `arji.json` still short-circuits the LLM.

**Story 3 — provenance.** Header strip with the absolute path, one-click copy, and an "Arij-managed clone" badge plus source link. The badge keys off `clone_source`, not the presence of a remote, so a user's own checkout of a GitHub repo isn't mislabelled.

The guard tests run against real git repositories in temp dirs — the story is about which directories vanish from disk, and a mocked `simple-git` can't show that. They cover symlink-escape, root-itself, and shared-prefix cases. One real defect surfaced and was fixed along the way: `simpleGit()` throws *synchronously* from its factory on a missing directory, which sat outside the guarded blocks in `detectDefaultBranch`.

## One thing you need to decide

This epic depends on a clone foundation that **isn't on `main`** — it's being built right now on four sibling branches. I implemented it so this branch compiles and tests standalone, which means `0027_project_clone_source.sql`, `lib/projects/workspace*.ts`, `lib/git/clone.ts` and `parseGitHubRepoInput` exist here *and* on those branches.

**Code Review**

# Code Review Report

## Findings

### 1. Critical — Pre-existing directories can be recursively deleted

**Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:156](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/git/clone.ts:156)

**Description:** Any non-empty destination without a readable origin is classified as `partial_clone`, including arbitrary directories, files, and valid local repositories without remotes. It is then recursively deleted before cloning. The tests currently codify this unsafe behavior.

**Recommendation:** Treat every existing destination as a conflict unless it is positively identified as the expected clone or carries a trusted Arij-created marker. Only clean up directories created by the current clone attempt.

### 2. Major — Concurrent clone requests can delete each other’s result

**Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:273](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/git/clone.ts:273)

**Description:** Classification, cloning, and cleanup are not serialized. Two requests can both observe an absent destination; when one clone subsequently fails because the other created it, its error handler deletes the shared destination.

**Recommendation:** Add a per-destination lock covering classification through completion. Cleanup must only remove a directory proven to have been created by that invocation.

### 3. Major — Clone ownership is client-writable

**Location:** [app/api/projects/[projectId]/route.ts:60](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/app/api/projects/[projectId]/route.ts:60)

**Description:** The generic PATCH route can set `cloneSource` to `"github"`, while deletion trusts that value as proof of ownership. A user-supplied project inside the projects root can therefore be reclassified and recursively removed. The generic creation route similarly trusts client-supplied provenance.

**Recommendation:** Make provenance immutable through PATCH and establish it through a trusted server-side clone handoff or durable pending-clone record.

### 4. Major — Cleanup can delete non-Arij worktrees

**Location:** [lib/projects/clone-cleanup.ts:158](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/projects/clone-cleanup.ts:158)

**Description:** Registered worktrees are deleted whenever they are anywhere beneath `projectsRoot`. The acceptance criterion limits removal to the clone’s `.arij-worktrees` entries. A manually created worktree elsewhere under the root, including uncommitted work, would be force-removed.

**Recommendation:** Require strict containment under the shared `.arij-worktrees` directory before either `git worktree remove` or `fs.rm`.

### 5. Major — First-time clones are not written to `git_sync_log`

**Location:** [app/api/projects/clone/route.ts:144](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/app/api/projects/clone/route.ts:144)

**Description:** A normal import has no project ID yet, so the function returns without creating an audit row. Consequently, almost every first-time clone and clone failure violates the requirement that each clone be recorded.

**Recommendation:** Make `git_sync_log.project_id` nullable and log pre-project operations with `NULL`, as already anticipated in the merge guidance.

### 6. Major — Persisted default branch is never consumed

**Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:331](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/git/clone.ts:331)

**Description:** `defaultBranch` is detected and stored, but no production code reads it. `lib/git/manager.ts` still guesses only `main` or `master`, so repositories using branches such as `develop` will clone successfully but fail during worktree creation or merging.

**Recommendation:** Thread the persisted branch through worktree, merge, and release operations, retaining the old guess only for legacy rows.

2. **DRY Principle:** No issues found.
3. **Error Handling:** Findings 1, 2, and 5.
4. **Performance:** No issues found.
5. **Naming Conventions:** No issues found.

8. **API Design:** Findings 3 and 5.

## Review findings addressed — 1 critical, 5 major

Commit `cae1682`. Full suite green: **2525 tests / 259 files**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint clean on every file touched (the one remaining warning in `lib/git/manager.ts` predates this branch).

### The critical finding and the ownership finding were the same bug

Nothing on disk distinguished a clone Arij made from a directory that merely sat where Arij would have put one. Classification guessed from `origin`; `clone_source` — the flag that authorises deletion — was a plain column any PATCH could set. Both are now settled by a fact rather than an inference: **`.git/arij-clone.json`**, written by the clone service into repositories it creates. Inside `.git` on purpose — git never shows it, it cannot be committed, and it dies with the repository it vouches for.

**1 (critical) — arbitrary directories deleted.** Anything Arij cannot positively identify is now `foreign_content`: a conflict reported to the user, never cleaned up on their behalf. Only two states let a clone proceed over existing content — a healthy clone of the requested repository (reused, non-destructive) or marked debris of Arij's own.

Rather than fixing the classification and keeping the delete, the download now runs into a staging sibling and moves into place with a single `rename`. The destination is never observably half-cloned, so the detect-and-delete-the-debris path is gone entirely, and a failed clone can only ever delete its own staging directory. Stale staging dirs are swept under the destination lock, where they are provably nobody's.

That also settles the story's "interrupted clone is reused, not reported as a conflict" criterion by construction instead of by heuristic: debris lands in staging, so the destination is either absent or a complete clone.

**2 (major) — concurrent clones.** Per-destination lock covering classify → clone → cleanup. In-process by design: Arij is one local server, and a lock file would add stale-lock recovery to solve a case that cannot occur here. Test drives two concurrent clones and asserts no overlap, one download, second call reuses.

**3 (major) — client-writable ownership.** `cloneSource` is gone from both request schemas; the create route derives it from the marker. A managed clone's `gitRepoPath` is frozen too — re-pointing it would carry deletion rights to a directory that never earned them. Removal re-checks the marker as a third gate behind the flag and root containment.

**4 (major) — non-Arij worktrees.** Cleanup now requires strict containment under the clone's `.arij-worktrees`. Registration to this clone is not a licence to delete; a hand-made worktree elsewhere may hold work that exists nowhere else.

**5 (major) — unaudited clones.** `git_sync_log.project_id` is nullable via hand-written `0028_git_sync_log_nullable_project.sql` (table rebuild following 0003/0012, journal `idx: 27`). Every clone is logged, first-time ones with `NULL`; an id naming no project degrades to unowned rather than losing the row to the FK. As flagged in the earlier merge note, this is the sibling branch's approach — worth keeping theirs if the numbering collides.

**6 (major) — unused `default_branch`.** New `resolveBaseBranch` replaces the `main`/`master` guess in `manager.ts` and `release.ts`: recorded branch → `origin/HEAD` → `main`/`master` → whatever exists. Threaded through all 14 worktree/merge/release call sites. Note this fixes `develop`-based repositories for **user-supplied** projects too, which never had a recorded branch to read.

The three that codified the unsafe replace now assert the refusal, and the `arij_debris` case is covered separately so the safe replace path is still pinned. The mocked `simple-git` in the reuse-flow tests was creating no directory, which the rename exposed — it now performs git's own side effect. Guard tests still run against real repositories in temp dirs; which directories survive is the entire claim, and a mock cannot demonstrate it.

The merge guidance still stands: this branch carries a clone foundation that is not on `main` and is being built on four sibling branches, and `epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC` / `epic-UY7xsxcNN41T` still both claim journal `idx: 26` independently of this work. **Code Review**

# Code Review Report

## Findings

### 1. Stored PAT is not used after the initial clone

- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `lib/git/clone.ts:282`
- **Description:** Reused repositories run an unauthenticated `fetchGitRemote(dest)` without the configured timeout or non-interactive environment. Since `origin` intentionally contains no credentials, private-repository re-imports can fail or hang. Subsequent push and tag operations have the same credential gap.
- **Recommendation:** Add a credential-aware git transport helper that injects `http.extraHeader` per command, disables prompts, supports cancellation, and redacts errors. Use it for fetch, pull, push, and tag operations. Add authenticated-reuse and timeout tests.

### 2. GitHub metadata can leak into a later local import

- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:314`
- **Description:** Switching back to “Local folder” does not clear `clone`. After cancelling a GitHub preview or encountering an analysis failure, a subsequent local import is created with the previous repository’s `cloneSource`, owner, remote URL, and branch.
- **Recommendation:** Clear clone provenance when selecting or starting a local import and when cancelling the preview. Prefer representing each analysis result together with its source metadata. Add a GitHub → cancel/error → local regression test.

### 3. Clone ownership and clean remote URL are client-authoritative

- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/route.ts:143`
- **Description:** Any existing directory can be submitted with `cloneSource: "github"`. Additionally, `gitRemoteUrl` is only length-checked, allowing credential-bearing URLs to be persisted despite the no-secret-on-disk contract.
- **Recommendation:** For clone metadata, require the normalized path to be within the managed root, parse and normalize the remote URL, reject userinfo, and verify owner/repository consistency. Add tests rejecting spoofed ownership and credential-bearing remotes.

### 4. Persisted default branch is not used

- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:53`
- **Description:** Worktree creation and merging still select `main`, otherwise unconditional `master`; PR creation separately defaults to `main`. Repositories whose default branch is `trunk` or `develop` import successfully but fail during normal Arij operations. Reused clones also report the currently checked-out branch rather than the remote default.
- **Recommendation:** Resolve the remote default from `origin/HEAD`, persist it, and use it for worktrees, merges, releases, diffs, and PR bases. Test with a repository whose only default branch is `trunk`.

### 5. Parser rejects harmless embedded consecutive dots

- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `lib/git/remote-parse.ts:75`
- **Description:** `segment.includes("..")` rejects names such as `repo..archive`. The specified traversal policy only requires rejecting the exact `.` and `..` components; separators are already excluded by the character validation.
- **Recommendation:** Reject only exact traversal components and add an accepted consecutive-dot repository case.

## Checklist Coverage

1. **Readability:** No issues found.
2. **DRY Principle:** No significant duplication found.
3. **Error Handling:** Findings 1 and 2.
4. **Performance:** No issues found. Full clones are intentional.
5. **Naming Conventions:** No issues found.
6. **Type Safety:** No issues found. TypeScript passes.
7. **Testing:** Coverage is extensive, but it misses the regressions described in Findings 1–4.
8. **API Design:** Findings 3–5.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false`: passed.
- Targeted ESLint run: passed.
- Vitest could not start in the read-only review sandbox because its worker directory under `/tmp` could not be created.
- Arij structured finding submission was attempted, but the connector required approval while this session’s approval policy is `never`.

## Summary

- Critical: 0
- Major: 4
- Minor: 1
- Suggestion: 0

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

**Revue traitée** — 5 constats sur 5 corrigés (commit `7f6f448`). Suite verte : `npm test` 2730 tests / 263 fichiers, `npm run test:e2e` 12 tests, `tsc --noEmit` propre.

| # | Constat | Traitement |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fetch de réutilisation non authentifié | corrigé |
| 2 | Fuite des métadonnées de clone vers un import local | corrigé |
| 3 | Propriété du clone décidée par le client | corrigé |
| 4 | Branche par défaut non utilisée | corrigé (voir réserve) |
| 5 | Points consécutifs refusés à tort | corrigé |

**1 — fetch authentifié et borné.** Le PAT est volontairement absent de `.git/config`, donc `fetchGitRemote()` sur le chemin de réutilisation partait sans identifiant : pour un dépôt privé, git demandait des identifiants sans terminal attaché — un blocage, pas une erreur. Le constructeur `-c http.extraHeader` est désormais partagé avec le clone, et le fetch porte le même timeout et `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

**2 — provenance liée à l'analyse.** `clone` survivait à une prévisualisation annulée, à une analyse en échec et au retour vers « Local folder ». La provenance voyage maintenant avec le résultat d'analyse et n'est posée que pour la prévisualisation à laquelle elle appartient. Trois tests de non-régression couvrent les trois chemins, plus la contre-épreuve que le cas GitHub légitime enregistre toujours sa provenance.

**3 — propriété vérifiée côté serveur.** `POST /api/projects` recalcule `<projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>` et refuse le drapeau pour tout autre chemin ; `gitRemoteUrl` est ré-analysée (une URL porteuse d'identifiants ne parse pas), stockée normalisée, et la cohérence owner/repo est vérifiée. `defaultBranch` est validée au niveau du schéma contre les formes que git refuse dans une réf.

**4 — branche par défaut.** `resolveRemoteDefaultBranch()` (`origin/HEAD`) est partagée par le service de clone, `manager.ts` et `release.ts` ; la convention `main`/`master` ne sert plus que de repli quand il n'y a pas de distant à interroger. La réponse du distant n'est retenue que si la branche existe localement — `main` seul ne résout pas `refs/remotes/origin/main`, on échangerait un échec contre un autre. Le clone rapporte cette branche plutôt que celle qui se trouve extraite dans un clone réutilisé.

⚠️ **Réserve assumée** : je n'ai pas étendu le transport authentifié à `pushGitBranch()` / `pullGitBranchWithConflictSupport()` / au tag de release, comme le suggérait la recommandation du constat 1. Ces fonctions préexistent à l'import et le débordement touchait l'orchestration git de toute l'application, hors périmètre d'un epic tests+doc. Le manque est documenté explicitement dans `docs/architecture/github-import.md` sous « Known gap » : un dépôt privé importé ainsi aura besoin d'un credential helper pour pousser. À arbitrer comme ticket dédié si vous le voulez couvert.

**5 — points consécutifs.** `repo..archive` est un nom GitHub légal et la classe de caractères exclut déjà tout séparateur ; seuls les composants exacts `.` et `..` sont de la traversée. En corrigeant le parseur j'ai trouvé la même sévérité excessive un cran plus bas : `validatePath()` refusait toute sous-chaîne `..`, ce qui aurait fait échouer l'import du clone que le parseur venait d'accepter. Les deux couches tracent maintenant la ligne au même endroit, et les charges utiles de traversée réelles restent refusées (103 tests sur le parseur).

Doc mise à jour en conséquence : le tableau des propriétés de sûreté, la section « Default branch », et la réserve ci-dessus.

comments.content:
All five review findings are fixed and the ticket is back in review (commit `7f6f448`).

## What the findings actually were

**Three were real defects in code this epic authored:**

- **Reuse fetch had no credentials, timeout, or prompt suppression.** Because the PAT is deliberately kept out of `.git/config`, the fetch on the reuse path was unauthenticated — a private-repo re-import blocked on a credential prompt with no terminal attached, which is a hang rather than an error. The `-c http.extraHeader` builder is now shared with the clone path.
- **Clone provenance leaked between imports.** `clone` state survived a cancelled preview, a failed analysis, and a switch back to "Local folder", so the next local import was created carrying the previous repo's `cloneSource`/owner/remote/branch. Provenance now travels with the analysis result.
- **`cloneSource` was client-authoritative.** It's the flag that later authorises Arij to delete a directory. The route now recomputes `<projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>` and refuses the claim for any other path, and re-parses `gitRemoteUrl` so a credential-bearing URL can't be persisted.

**One was a pre-existing bug the import surfaced:** `createWorktree`/`mergeWorktree` guessed `main`-else-`master`, so a `trunk` or `develop` repo imported cleanly and then failed at `worktree add`. All call sites now resolve `origin/HEAD` through a shared helper.

## Two things worth flagging

**I found a second instance of finding 5.** Fixing the parser to accept `repo..archive` (legal on GitHub; the character class already excludes separators) exposed that `validatePath()` rejected *any* `..` substring — so a clone the parser had just accepted would have failed at import. Both layers now draw the line at exact `.`/`..` components. Real traversal payloads stay rejected.

**I deliberately did not do part of finding 1.** The reviewer recommended a credential-aware transport for push, pull, and tag as well. Those functions predate the import flow and rewiring them touches the whole app's git orchestration — well outside a tests-and-docs epic, with real regression risk. I fixed the reuse fetch, which is the path this epic owns, and documented the remainder as a "Known gap" in `docs/architecture/github-import.md`: a private repo imported this way needs a credential helper to push. That's a judgement call on scope, so it's yours to overrule — say the word and I'll do it as a follow-up.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Project: Arij

## Project Specification

# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

Arij is a local-first web app that lets you plan, organize, and build software projects using AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code). You describe features as epics; Arij orchestrates the agents, manages git branches and worktrees, runs reviews, and merges the result. Everything runs on your machine — no cloud, no account, no telemetry.

---

## 1. Objectives of this iteration

Today a project can only be attached to a directory that **already exists on disk** (`app/projects/new/page.tsx` and `app/projects/import/page.tsx` both ask for a filesystem path, validated by `lib/validation/path.ts`, which requires an existing directory). Arij never clones anything.

This iteration adds a third entry point: **import a project directly from a GitHub URL**. Arij clones the repository into an app-managed workspace directory and then works from that clone exactly as it would from a user-supplied local repo.

Goals:

1. Paste `https://github.com/owner/repo` (or `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, or `owner/repo`) in the Import flow and get a fully set-up Arij project.
2. Clone into a predictable, app-managed root — `<arij>/projects/` by default, overridable in Settings.
3. Support private repositories using the GitHub PAT already stored in the `settings` table (`github_pat`), **without ever persisting the token to disk**.
4. Reuse the entire existing import pipeline unchanged: Claude analysis, `arji.json` short-circuit, epic/story creation, `arji.json` export.
5. Auto-populate `githubOwnerRepo` so push / PR / release / issue-sync features work immediately, with no manual "Connect GitHub" step.

## 2. Constraints

- **Migrations are hand-written.** `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run: the `meta/*_snapshot.json` files stop at 0013 while the journal reaches 0026, so generate would produce a wrong diff. The new migration is authored by hand as `0027_project_clone_source.sql` and appended to `meta/_journal.json` at `idx: 26`.
- **Full clones only.** Arij creates worktrees, branches, merges and tags (`lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/git/release.ts`). A shallow clone (`--depth`) would break `worktree add` from `main` and merge-base computation. No `--depth`, no `--single-branch`.
- **No new git library.** `simple-git@^3.30` is the only git dependency; `@octokit/rest@^22` is the only GitHub API client. The `gh` CLI is not used anywhere and must not be introduced.
- **No new job infrastructure.** The existing import already blocks on a multi-minute `POST /api/projects/import` call. Clone follows the same synchronous request/response shape; only the UI gains a distinct progress step.
- **Credentials live in SQLite, not env.** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is documented in the README but unused in code; the real source is `getGitHubTokenFromSettings()` in `lib/github/client.ts`.

## 3. Technical stack

Unchanged: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui, SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle, `simple-git`, `@octokit/rest`, nanoid IDs, Vitest + Playwright.

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Workspace layout

```
<arij>/
  data/                  # DB, session logs, uploads (gitignored)
  projects/              # NEW — app-managed clone root (gitignored)
    <owner>-<repo>/      # the clone; becomes projects.git_repo_path
    .arij-worktrees/     # created automatically by createWorktree()
```

`lib/git/manager.ts:37` places worktrees at `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")`. With a clone at `projects/<owner>-<repo>`, worktrees land in `projects/.arij-worktrees` — no change to the worktree code is required, but `/projects` must be added to `.gitignore` so Arij's own repo stays clean when dogfooding.

The root is resolved by a new `lib/projects/workspace.ts`, reading the `projects_root` settings key with a `<cwd>/projects` default. Following the established convention (`lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts`, `lib/night/constants.ts`), the key name, default and parser live in a client-safe `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` that does not import `db`.

### 4.2 Request flow

```
User pastes GitHub URL
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/clone            <-- NEW
  parse URL -> { owner, repo }
  resolve dest = <projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>
  if dest exists && origin matches  -> reuse (fetch only)
  else git clone (token via -c http.extraHeader)
  -> { path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/import           <-- EXISTING, unchanged
  validatePath(path) -> arji.json short-circuit OR Claude analysis
  -> { preview, path, fromExistingFile }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects                  <-- EXISTING, + githubOwnerRepo/clone metadata
PATCH /api/projects/:id, epics, user-stories, sync export
```

Splitting clone from analysis keeps `POST /api/projects/import` untouched and gives the UI two honest progress steps ("Cloning…" then "Analyzing…") instead of one opaque spinner.

### 4.3 URL parsing

`lib/git/remote.ts` already exports `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`, covering `git@github.com:`, `ssh://`, `https://`, `git://`. A new `parseGitHubRepoInput()` wraps it and additionally accepts the shorthand `owner/repo` and browser URLs carrying a suffix (`/tree/main`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme`). Owner and repo are then re-validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and rejected if either is `.` or `..`, so a crafted URL can never escape the clone root.

### 4.4 Credential handling

The clone runs as:

```
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:PAT)>" \
    clone --no-tags=false <clean-https-url> <dest>
```

Because the header is passed with `-c` it is never written to `.git/config`; `origin` keeps the clean URL, so subsequent `fetch`/`pull`/`push` behave exactly like a hand-made clone and no secret is stored on disk. Any error string returned to the client is passed through a redaction helper that strips `Basic <...>` and `://user:pass@` fragments before it reaches the UI or `git_sync_log`. Public repositories clone with no token at all.

### 4.5 Data model

`projects` gains three nullable columns (migration `0027`):

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clone_source` | `"github"` when Arij created the directory, `NULL` for user-supplied paths |
| `git_remote_url` | the clean clone URL, for display and re-clone |
| `default_branch` | branch reported by the clone, used instead of the `main`/`master` guess |

`clone_source` is the ownership flag: only directories Arij created may be offered for deletion when a project is deleted. Existing rows keep `NULL` and behave exactly as today.

### 4.6 Observability

Each clone writes a `git_sync_log` row with `operation = "clone"` (the column is free-form text, so no schema change is needed) recording the owner/repo, destination, duration, whether the clone was reused, and the redacted error on failure.

## 5. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Clone root defaults to `<cwd>/projects`, configurable via `projects_root` | Matches the user's request; the setting keeps users who store code elsewhere in control. |
| Destination is `<owner>-<repo>` | Deterministic and collision-free across owners; makes re-import idempotent. |
| Existing directory with a matching `origin` is reused (fetch, no re-clone) | Same idempotent posture as `createWorktree()`; re-running an import is cheap and safe. Mismatched remote returns 409 rather than silently overwriting. |
| Token injected via `-c http.extraHeader`, not embedded in the remote URL | A token baked into `origin` would persist in `.git/config` forever and leak through every diff/log surface. |
| Clone is a separate endpoint, not a flag on `/api/projects/import` | Keeps the analysis route untouched, gives real progress steps, and makes clone independently testable. |
| No shallow clone | Worktrees, merges and tags need full history. |
| Partial clone on failure is deleted | Avoids a half-clone being reused later as a "matching" repo. |

## 6. Out of scope

Non-GitHub hosts (GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted), SSH-key-based clones of private repos, background/queued cloning with cancellation, and monorepo sub-directory imports. The parsing layer is written so a second host can be added later without touching the clone service.

# Project: Arij

## Project Specification

# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

Arij is a local-first web app that lets you plan, organize, and build software projects using AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code). You describe features as epics; Arij orchestrates the agents, manages git branches and worktrees, runs reviews, and merges the result. Everything runs on your machine — no cloud, no account, no telemetry.

---

## 1. Objectives of this iteration

Today a project can only be attached to a directory that **already exists on disk** (`app/projects/new/page.tsx` and `app/projects/import/page.tsx` both ask for a filesystem path, validated by `lib/validation/path.ts`, which requires an existing directory). Arij never clones anything.

This iteration adds a third entry point: **import a project directly from a GitHub URL**. Arij clones the repository into an app-managed workspace directory and then works from that clone exactly as it would from a user-supplied local repo.

Goals:

1. Paste `https://github.com/owner/repo` (or `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, or `owner/repo`) in the Import flow and get a fully set-up Arij project.
2. Clone into a predictable, app-managed root — `<arij>/projects/` by default, overridable in Settings.
3. Support private repositories using the GitHub PAT already stored in the `settings` table (`github_pat`), **without ever persisting the token to disk**.
4. Reuse the entire existing import pipeline unchanged: Claude analysis, `arji.json` short-circuit, epic/story creation, `arji.json` export.
5. Auto-populate `githubOwnerRepo` so push / PR / release / issue-sync features work immediately, with no manual "Connect GitHub" step.

## 2. Constraints

- **Migrations are hand-written.** `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run: the `meta/*_snapshot.json` files stop at 0013 while the journal reaches 0026, so generate would produce a wrong diff. The new migration is authored by hand as `0027_project_clone_source.sql` and appended to `meta/_journal.json` at `idx: 26`.
- **Full clones only.** Arij creates worktrees, branches, merges and tags (`lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/git/release.ts`). A shallow clone (`--depth`) would break `worktree add` from `main` and merge-base computation. No `--depth`, no `--single-branch`.
- **No new git library.** `simple-git@^3.30` is the only git dependency; `@octokit/rest@^22` is the only GitHub API client. The `gh` CLI is not used anywhere and must not be introduced.
- **No new job infrastructure.** The existing import already blocks on a multi-minute `POST /api/projects/import` call. Clone follows the same synchronous request/response shape; only the UI gains a distinct progress step.
- **Credentials live in SQLite, not env.** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is documented in the README but unused in code; the real source is `getGitHubTokenFromSettings()` in `lib/github/client.ts`.

## 3. Technical stack

Unchanged: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui, SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle, `simple-git`, `@octokit/rest`, nanoid IDs, Vitest + Playwright.

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Workspace layout

```
<arij>/
  data/                  # DB, session logs, uploads (gitignored)
  projects/              # NEW — app-managed clone root (gitignored)
    <owner>-<repo>/      # the clone; becomes projects.git_repo_path
    .arij-worktrees/     # created automatically by createWorktree()
```

`lib/git/manager.ts:37` places worktrees at `path.join(repoPath, "..", ".arij-worktrees")`. With a clone at `projects/<owner>-<repo>`, worktrees land in `projects/.arij-worktrees` — no change to the worktree code is required, but `/projects` must be added to `.gitignore` so Arij's own repo stays clean when dogfooding.

The root is resolved by a new `lib/projects/workspace.ts`, reading the `projects_root` settings key with a `<cwd>/projects` default. Following the established convention (`lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts`, `lib/night/constants.ts`), the key name, default and parser live in a client-safe `lib/projects/workspace-constants.ts` that does not import `db`.

### 4.2 Request flow

```
User pastes GitHub URL
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/clone            <-- NEW
  parse URL -> { owner, repo }
  resolve dest = <projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>
  if dest exists && origin matches  -> reuse (fetch only)
  else git clone (token via -c http.extraHeader)
  -> { path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects/import           <-- EXISTING, unchanged
  validatePath(path) -> arji.json short-circuit OR Claude analysis
  -> { preview, path, fromExistingFile }
        |
        v
POST /api/projects                  <-- EXISTING, + githubOwnerRepo/clone metadata
PATCH /api/projects/:id, epics, user-stories, sync export
```

Splitting clone from analysis keeps `POST /api/projects/import` untouched and gives the UI two honest progress steps ("Cloning…" then "Analyzing…") instead of one opaque spinner.

### 4.3 URL parsing

`lib/git/remote.ts` already exports `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`, covering `git@github.com:`, `ssh://`, `https://`, `git://`. A new `parseGitHubRepoInput()` wraps it and additionally accepts the shorthand `owner/repo` and browser URLs carrying a suffix (`/tree/main`, `/pull/12`, `?tab=readme`). Owner and repo are then re-validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and rejected if either is `.` or `..`, so a crafted URL can never escape the clone root.

### 4.4 Credential handling

The clone runs as:

```
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:PAT)>" \
    clone --no-tags=false <clean-https-url> <dest>
```

Because the header is passed with `-c` it is never written to `.git/config`; `origin` keeps the clean URL, so subsequent `fetch`/`pull`/`push` behave exactly like a hand-made clone and no secret is stored on disk. Any error string returned to the client is passed through a redaction helper that strips `Basic <...>` and `://user:pass@` fragments before it reaches the UI or `git_sync_log`. Public repositories clone with no token at all.

### 4.5 Data model

`projects` gains three nullable columns (migration `0027`):

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clone_source` | `"github"` when Arij created the directory, `NULL` for user-supplied paths |
| `git_remote_url` | the clean clone URL, for display and re-clone |
| `default_branch` | branch reported by the clone, used instead of the `main`/`master` guess |

`clone_source` is the ownership flag: only directories Arij created may be offered for deletion when a project is deleted. Existing rows keep `NULL` and behave exactly as today.

### 4.6 Observability

Each clone writes a `git_sync_log` row with `operation = "clone"` (the column is free-form text, so no schema change is needed) recording the owner/repo, destination, duration, whether the clone was reused, and the redacted error on failure.

## 5. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Clone root defaults to `<cwd>/projects`, configurable via `projects_root` | Matches the user's request; the setting keeps users who store code elsewhere in control. |
| Destination is `<owner>-<repo>` | Deterministic and collision-free across owners; makes re-import idempotent. |
| Existing directory with a matching `origin` is reused (fetch, no re-clone) | Same idempotent posture as `createWorktree()`; re-running an import is cheap and safe. Mismatched remote returns 409 rather than silently overwriting. |
| Token injected via `-c http.extraHeader`, not embedded in the remote URL | A token baked into `origin` would persist in `.git/config` forever and leak through every diff/log surface. |
| Clone is a separate endpoint, not a flag on `/api/projects/import` | Keeps the analysis route untouched, gives real progress steps, and makes clone independently testable. |
| No shallow clone | Worktrees, merges and tags need full history. |
| Partial clone on failure is deleted | Avoids a half-clone being reused later as a "matching" repo. |

## 6. Out of scope

Non-GitHub hosts (GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted), SSH-key-based clones of private repos, background/queued cloning with cancellation, and monorepo sub-directory imports. The parsing layer is written so a second host can be added later without touching the clone service.

 * cannot be bundled for the browser — so the import page can validate what the
 * user pastes with the exact same rules the clone route applies server-side.

 * no I/O of any kind.
 *

 * from a single place.

export interface ParsedGitHubRemote {
  owner: string;
  repo: string;
  ownerRepo: string;
}

export interface ParsedGitHubRepoInput extends ParsedGitHubRemote {
  /** Always normalised to https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git */
  cloneUrl: string;
}

export function normalizeRemoteUrl(raw: string): string {
  return raw.trim();
}

export function parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl(
  remoteUrl: string
): ParsedGitHubRemote | null {
  const value = normalizeRemoteUrl(remoteUrl);
  if (!value) return null;

  const patterns = [
    /^git@github\.com:(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
    /^ssh:\/\/git@github\.com\/(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
    /^https?:\/\/(?:www\.)?github\.com\/(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
    /^git:\/\/github\.com\/(?<owner>[^/]+)\/(?<repo>[^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/i,
  ];

  for (const pattern of patterns) {
    const match = value.match(pattern);
    if (!match?.groups?.owner || !match.groups.repo) {
      continue;
    }

    const owner = match.groups.owner;
    const repo = match.groups.repo;
    if (!owner || !repo) continue;

    return {
      owner,
      repo,
      ownerRepo: `${owner}/${repo}`,
    };
  }

  return null;
}

 * GitHub allows letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_` in owner and repo names.
 * Anything else — separators, NUL bytes, whitespace — is rejected here so a
 * crafted URL can never reach the filesystem layer. A leading `-` is refused
 * as well: it would otherwise be read as an option by `git clone`.
 */
const REPO_SEGMENT_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/;

  if (!segment) return false;
  if (segment.startsWith("-")) return false;
  // Only the exact `.` and `..` components traverse. Dots *inside* a name are
  // ordinary GitHub characters (`repo..archive` is a legal repository), and the
  // character class below already excludes every separator, so an embedded `..`
  // cannot climb out of the clone root. Matches assertSegment() in
  // lib/projects/workspace.ts, which draws the line in the same place.
  if (segment === "." || segment === "..") return false;
  return REPO_SEGMENT_PATTERN.test(segment);
}

  owner: string,
  repo: string
): ParsedGitHubRepoInput | null {
  const cleanRepo = repo.replace(/\.git$/i, "");
  if (!isSafeRepoSegment(owner) || !isSafeRepoSegment(cleanRepo)) {
    return null;

  return {
    owner,
    repo: cleanRepo,
    ownerRepo: `${owner}/${cleanRepo}`,
    cloneUrl: `https://github.com/${owner}/${cleanRepo}.git`,

 * shorthand — into a normalised clone target. Returns null for anything that
 * is not a GitHub repository or whose owner/repo fails strict validation.

  input: string

  if (typeof input !== "string") return null;
