comments.content:
**Code Review**

Plan mode is still active, so `submit_findings` is blocked — the full report is below and I can file it verbatim the moment plan mode is off.

# Code Review — Direct Chat via OpenAI-Compatible API (Fast Mode)

**Branch:** `feature/epic-r8-sbLpkREWJ-direct-chat-via-openai-compatible-api-fa` (7 commits, `3f4bf64..c7f28f8`, 29 files, +2877/−184)
**Baseline verified locally:** `__tests__/chat-stream-route.test.ts`, `chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts`, `openai-client.test.ts`, `settings-openai-section.test.tsx` — **52/52 passing**.

All six stories' acceptance criteria are implemented, and the previous round's three Major findings are genuinely fixed (API-key wipe on Save, user message persisted before the 400 backstops, `@document` mentions no-op), along with partial-content discard, raw provider ids, and staged attachments. One new blocking regression was introduced by the fix commit.

---

## 1. Readability

Good. The `lib/openai/constants.ts` (client-safe) / `client.ts` (server-only) split matches `lib/night/constants.ts`, comments explain *why* (the `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_PROVIDER` "deliberately NOT an `AgentProvider`" note, the `normalizeProvider` allowlist rationale), and `saveAssistantAndTitle` is now declared at line 215 *above* the fast-mode branch, resolving the forward-reference the last review flagged.

## 2. DRY Principle

Resolved. `sseResponse()` (route.ts:62) replaces the four verbatim `text/event-stream` response literals. `buildChatCompletionsUrl` / `buildOpenAiHeaders` / `buildChatCompletionsBody` are shared between the test and stream paths. No new duplication.

## 3. Error Handling

### 🔴 Critical — the CLI prompt no longer contains the message the user just sent
**`app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts:177`** (read at 168-175, insert at 193-202)

`c7f28f8` correctly hoisted the fast-mode validation above the user-message insert — but it carried the `recentMessages` query up with it. On `main` the insert ran first, so `messageHistory` included the current turn. It no longer does (better-sqlite3 is synchronous; the read at 168 completes before the insert at 193).

The fast-mode branch compensates, appending `userContent` explicitly at line 311. **The CLI branches do not:**

- `buildChatPrompt(project, [], messageHistory, chatSystemPrompt)` (line 421) — the builder's own instruction is *"Answer the user's latest message"*, and `chatHistorySection(messages)` is its only source of that message (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:147-151`).
- `buildEpicRefinementPrompt` / `buildEpicFinalizationPrompt` (lines 404-418) — same.
- `effectivePrompt = resumeSession ? userContent : prompt` (line 447) — only the *resume* path still carries the message.

*Failure scenario:* conversations are created without a `cliSessionId` (`conversations/route.ts` never sets one), so `resumeSession` is false on the first message of every conversation. A user opens a new brainstorm tab on Claude Code and asks "How should I structure auth?" — the prompt is assembled from an empty history plus "Answer the user's latest message", with no message present. For non-resumable providers (`codex`, `qwen-code`, `deepseek`, `zai` per `lib/agent-sessions/resume-capability.ts`) **every** turn answers the previous question.

*Recommendation:* append the current turn to `messageHistory` after the insert (or move the read back below it), keeping the fast-mode branch's explicit append. See §7 for why the suite stays green through this.

### 🟠 Major — killing a fast-mode chat from the Agent Monitor hangs the browser
**`route.ts:352-357`**

The abort branch unregisters the activity, resets the status, and `return`s — without `controller.close()`. The `ReadableStream` never terminates and the HTTP response stays open.

Harmless for a client disconnect (`cancel()` already ran, nobody is reading). But `DELETE /api/projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId` → `activityRegistry.cancel(id)` → `kill()` → `abortController.abort()` fires while the browser is still connected. `hooks/useChat.ts:126-128` exits its loop only on stream end, so `sending` stays true and the empty assistant bubble persists until reload. Every CLI branch closes on kill (the spawn promise resolves → `saveAssistantAndTitle` → `controller.close()`); this branch is the only divergence.

*Recommendation:* set a `clientCancelled` flag inside `cancel()` and `controller.close()` on abort when it is false — closing after a client cancel throws `TypeError: Invalid state`.

### 🟡 Minor — no timeout on the streaming path *(carried over, not addressed)*
**`lib/openai/client.ts:326`** — `testOpenAiConnection` has a 15 s `AbortController` (line 225); `streamOpenAiChatCompletion` passes only the caller's signal. A server that accepts and never responds pins the conversation at `generating` and leaves the activity registered. Story 6 names *timeout* as a failure mode, and `describeNetworkError`'s "request timed out." branch is currently unreachable from chat. Compounds with the finding above: the only escape is the kill button, which hangs the client.

### 🟡 Minor — the Base URL is echoed verbatim into a persisted chat message
**`lib/openai/client.ts:324`** — the invalid-URL error embeds `config.baseUrl`, which the route stores as the assistant message body. Providers that document key-in-URL forms (`https://<token>@host/v1`) would put a credential into `chat_messages` — the one leak in an otherwise clean credential story. Strip userinfo before interpolating.

**Fixed since last review:** partial output is now preserved on mid-stream failure (365-368), `@mention` enrichment runs in fast mode (288-299), the Base URL is validated before the streaming fetch (319-325), `rawText` stops buffering once `sawSseDataLine` is set (354-356), and the decoder is flushed (369-373).

## 4. Performance

No N+1 queries, no missing indexes, no large payloads. `getOpenAiConfigFromSettings()` is 4 point lookups on a KV table. The `rawText`/decoder-flush suggestions from the last round are both applied.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found.

## 6. Type Safety

No `any`. The DB `role` column is now narrowed properly (`route.ts:178`) instead of cast onto the wire. `getProvider(resolvedAgent.provider as ProviderType)` (line 468) remains, but is sound and commented — the fast-mode branch returns above it.

I re-verified that widening `PROVIDER_LABELS` to `Record<ChatModeProvider, string>` is safe: 13 consumers, all index by key, zero `Object.keys`/`Object.entries` iteration — so `openai-compatible` cannot leak into a build or review provider picker. `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` and `PROVIDER_TIERS` are untouched.

## 7. Testing

Coverage of the new module is strong — 19 client tests (SSE split-chunk, `\r\n`, `[DONE]`, non-streaming fallback, invalid URL without fetch), 14 route tests, 8 Settings-section tests including the two regression tests the last review asked for (save-without-retyping-key, explicit clear).

**Gap that let the Critical through — `__tests__/chat-stream-route.test.ts:264`:** `expect.any(Array)` for the history argument, combined with `buildChatPrompt.mockReturnValue("CHAT_PROMPT")`, means the suite cannot observe what the CLI branches send to the agent; the db mock replays a fixed `allQueue` regardless of insert ordering. Assert the last history entry equals the posted content, in both the epic-refinement and brainstorm cases.

Two smaller gaps: no test that a monitor-initiated `activityRegistry.cancel()` ends the fast-mode stream, and none that the "Test connection" button is disabled while in flight (an explicit acceptance criterion — implemented at `app/settings/page.tsx`, uncovered).

## 8. API Design

🟡 **Minor — `app/api/settings/openai/test/route.ts:18`** *(carried over, not addressed)*: every failure returns `400`, including upstream `401`, connection refused, and timeout. The route it mirrors (`app/api/settings/github/validate/route.ts`) returns `400` only for missing input and `401` for a rejected token. Use `400` for config errors, `401` for upstream auth, `502` for connectivity — `__tests__/settings-openai-test-route.test.ts:61,75` encode the current 400s and need updating with it.

Otherwise consistent: `{ data }` / `{ error }` throughout, SSE headers identical to the CLI branches, and the key genuinely never leaves the server (masked as `{ hasToken }` in `GET`, read server-side in the test route, `Bearer` only when set).

## Cross-cutting: UI

🟡 **Minor — chat tabs are never auto-titled (`route.ts:246`)**: title generation is gated on `label === "Brainstorm" || "New Epic"`, but `ChatTabBar.tsx:118` creates the new tab with `label: "Chat"` — so every tab in the bar reads "Chat". Related: `resolveLegacyConversationLabel` (`lib/chat/parity-contract.ts:39`) falls back to `"Brainstorm"` for a label-less conversation, now wrong for the `chat` type this epic introduces.

🟡 **Minor — staged attachments are hidden, not cleared (`MessageInput.tsx:129`)**: `effectiveAttachments` correctly stops them being previewed or sent, closing the 400. But `attachments` state survives — the uploads stay orphaned in `chat_attachments`, and switching back to a CLI provider makes them silently reappear and send.

ℹ️ **`app/settings/page.tsx:604`** — `handleClearOpenAiKey` reuses `savingOpenAi`, so "Clear key" flips the unrelated **Save** button to "Saving…".

**Fixed since last review:** the four `providerLabel` helpers now resolve via `isChatProvider`, so the monitor shows "OpenAI-compatible" rather than the raw id.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | 1 | CLI prompts lost the current user message (ordering regression in `c7f28f8`) |
| **Major** | 1 | Monitor kill leaves the fast-mode SSE response open — browser hangs |
| **Minor** | 6 | No streaming timeout; `400` for upstream failures; Base URL echoed into chat history; chat tabs never titled; staged attachments not cleared; parity label fallback |
| **Info** | 2 | Shared `savingOpenAi` flag; three test gaps |

The feature work is solid and the previous round's findings were properly resolved rather than papered over. The blocker is collateral from the fix itself: hoisting validation above the user-message insert also moved the history read, and only the new fast-mode branch was updated to compensate — the CLI paths silently regressed, invisibly to a suite that mocks the prompt builder. It's a two-line fix plus one tightened assertion.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: Full Auto Mode: Standing Build / Review / Merge Supervisor
epics.description:
## Contexte

Arij dispose déjà de deux modes autonomes, mais ce sont tous les deux des rafales one-shot :
- `lib/pipeline/` fait passer *un* ticket par build → review → auto-fix puis s'arrête.
- `lib/night/` fait *une* passe DAG sur un lot d'epics puis se termine.

Aucun ne surveille le board en continu. Le mode Full Auto est le chaînon manquant : un superviseur permanent, activé par projet, avec des budgets de concurrence indépendants pour la build et la review.

Une fois activé, Arij en continu :
- build tout ce qui est en `todo`, plus tout ce qui est en `in_progress` sans agent dessus (ticket revenu d'une review négative) ;
- review tout ce qui est en `review` ;
- merge un ticket dès que sa review est propre.

## Décisions validées avec l'utilisateur

| Question | Réponse |
|---|---|
| Périmètre des tickets | Tous les tickets — epics, bugs et user stories |
| Merge après une review propre | Oui, le mode auto merge |
| Portée d'activation | Par projet |
| Si build+review > budget scheduler | Avertir seulement — ne jamais le remonter silencieusement |

## Réutilisation (ne rien réécrire)

| Besoin | Existant | Chemin |
|---|---|---|
| Dispatch build/review programmatique | `createPipelineStageDriver(...).launchStage({stage})` — « réplique les closures des routes au byte près pour que le board ne puisse pas distinguer une étape de pipeline d'un dispatch humain ». Supporte `scope: 'epic' \| 'story'`. | `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:140` |
| Primitive de merge | `mergeWorktree(gitRepoPath, branchName, worktreePath)` → `{merged, commitHash, error}` | `lib/git/manager.ts` |
| Porte « la review est OK » | Les gardes `→ done` du moteur de workflow | `lib/workflow/engine.ts:49-97` |
| Transition validée + event + log | `applyTransition({... source:'merge'})` | `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts:47` |
| « Un agent est-il déjà sur ce ticket ? » | `getRunningSessionForTarget(target)` — compte `queued` + `running` | `lib/agents/concurrency.ts:94` |
| « Ce ticket attend-il un humain ? » | `isAwaitingReply(signal)` — pur, client-safe | `lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts:30` |
| Budget de slots + file FIFO | `agentScheduler.submit(projectId, sessionId, launch)` | `lib/agents/scheduler.ts:124` |
| Patron de boucle permanente | Watchdog : singleton globalThis, `start()` idempotent, interval `unref()`, `sweep(now)` pur pour les tests | `lib/agents/watchdog.ts` |
| Patron de registre mémoire | `NightRunRegistry` — map active + ring récent, pas de table | `lib/night/registry.ts` |
| Convention constantes client-safe | clé + fn clé par projet + défaut + `parseX` renvoyant `null` pour tomber au niveau suivant | `lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts` |
| Wiring au boot | `register()` dans `instrumentation.ts` (démarre déjà le watchdog) | `instrumentation.ts` |
| UI sélecteur agent + concurrence | `NightRunDialog` compose déjà `NamedAgentSelect` + `Input` de concurrence + `OptionRow` | `components/night/NightRunDialog.tsx` |

## La machine à états boucle déjà toute seule

Vérifié dans `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` :
- lancement build → epic `→ in_progress`, branche créée (`:585`)
- build réussie → epic `→ review` (`:745`)
- verdict de review négatif → epic `→ in_progress` (`:916`), sans agent dessus
- verdict positif → l'epic reste en `review`

Le superviseur ne fait que dispatcher ; c'est le driver qui déplace les tickets. Un ticket rejeté retombe en `in_progress` sans agent et est naturellement repris au sweep suivant.

## Granularité : « tous les tickets » face à une branche par epic

Git est la contrainte. Il y a un worktree et une branche par epic — la route de build story écrit `epics.branchName` et réutilise le worktree de l'epic, et `getRunningSessionForTarget` en scope story matche aussi les sessions de l'epic parent (`lib/agents/concurrency.ts:65-70`), donc deux stories du même epic ne peuvent jamais tourner en parallèle. Cette garde existe déjà ; le mode auto en hérite gratuitement.

Règle retenue :
- Build → scope story quand l'epic a des stories (une à la fois par epic, plein d'epics en parallèle) ; scope epic sinon. La route de build story promeut déjà l'epic en `review` quand toutes les stories sœurs sont review/done (`stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:303-330`).
- Review et merge → toujours au scope epic. La branche est l'unité d'intégration et `epic.branchName` est ce qui se merge. Reviewer chaque story *puis* l'epic doublerait le coût en tokens pour le même diff.

## Les quatre pièges à traiter

1. Re-review infinie. Une review qui passe laisse l'epic en `review`. Un balayage naïf le re-reviewerait sans fin. → Un epic en `review` n'est candidat que s'il n'a aucune session de review terminale plus récente que sa dernière session de code terminale. Délibérément temporel, pas basé sur le verdict : le verdict est une heuristique de sous-chaîne sur le markdown de l'agent (`epics/[epicId]/review/route.ts:337`), sans champ structuré.

2. Écraser une question d'agent. Un agent finissant en `asked_question` laisse le ticket maintenu en `in_progress` par `handleAskedQuestionOutcome` (`lib/workflow/agent-question.ts:42`) — indiscernable de « revient de review » pour un sélecteur naïf. → Exclure tout ticket où `isAwaitingReply(...)` est vrai ; il redevient éligible dès que l'utilisateur répond par un commentaire.

3. Merger quelque chose qui n'est pas réellement approuvé. « Review OK » n'existe comme booléen nulle part. → Ne pas en inventer un. `applyTransition(→ done, source:'merge')` refuse déjà tant que `hasCompletedReview` est faux *ou* que `hasOpenReviewComments` est vrai (`lib/workflow/engine.ts:51-63`). Le mode auto tente la transition et traite un refus comme « pas prêt, on passe ». Sa propre porte est *plus stricte* que celle du moteur, car la fraîcheur du piège 1 compense le fait que `hasCompletedReview` est laxiste (`lib/workflow/context.ts:32-51`). → Ne surtout pas réutiliser `POST .../approve` : il résout en masse tous les commentaires de review ouverts (`approve/route.ts:30-38`), écrasant exactement les findings bloquants qui doivent empêcher un merge auto.

4. Double comptage des budgets. Build (N) + review (M) vivent *au-dessus* du budget `agent_max_concurrent` par projet (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts:81`, défaut 3). Si N+M le dépasse, le mode admet du travail qui s'empile dans la file FIFO — et comme `getRunningSessionForTarget` compte les `queued`, le board paraît occupé sans rien exécuter. → Admission control sur ses propres sessions en vol, et avertissement dans le dialog quand N+M dépasse le budget (décision utilisateur : avertir seulement).

## Plan d'implémentation

Aucune migration. Toute la config vit dans la table clé/valeur `settings` existante et chaque session dispatchée est une ligne `agent_sessions` ordinaire.

1. `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` (client-safe, sans import `db`) — clés par projet avec repli global : `auto_mode_enabled:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_build_agent:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_build_concurrency:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_review_agent:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_review_concurrency:<projectId>`. Plus `DEFAULT_AUTO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY = 2`, `DEFAULT_AUTO_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 1`, `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000`, parsers renvoyant `null`, `resolveAutoModeConfig(settingsMap, projectId)` pour l'UI, chaînes de raison d'activity-log préfixées `"Auto mode "`, et `AUTO_RUN_ID_PREFIX = "auto_"` pour tamponner `batchRunId`.
2. `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` — résolveur serveur par projet → global → défaut, copie de `resolveMaxConcurrentForProject`.
3. `lib/auto-mode/select.ts` — les trois sélecteurs (build, review, merge) avec toutes les exclusions.
4. `lib/auto-mode/registry.ts` — état mémoire globalThis + map de parking.
5. `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts` — `tryAutoMerge(projectId, epicId)`.
6. `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts` — le sweep avec mutex par projet.
7. Extension du driver : ajouter `reviewNamedAgentId` optionnel à `PipelineStageDriverInit`.
8. `instrumentation.ts` — `startAutoMode()` + chaînage du hook terminal.
9. `app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts` — GET/PUT.
10. `components/auto-mode/AutoModeDialog.tsx` + toggle dans la toolbar du board.

## Hors périmètre

Reviews par story (les stories sont des unités de travail, les epics des unités d'intégration), switch global multi-projets, table persistée pour l'état du mode, planification horaire (le mode est ON/OFF, pas « de 22h à 6h »).

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want auto-mode configuration stored in the settings table with a client-safe constants module, so that I can enable the mode per project and tune agents and concurrency without a schema migration
user_stories.description: Create `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` following the exact convention established by `lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts` and `lib/pipeline/constants.ts`: a header comment explaining why the file is split, the global setting key, a `<key>:<projectId>` per-project override function, defaults with an inclusive clamp range, and a `parseX` returning `null` for "not configured" so callers fall through the chain. The five keys are `auto_mode_enabled`, `auto_mode_build_agent`, `auto_mode_build_concurrency`, `auto_mode_review_agent`, `auto_mode_review_concurrency`. Also export `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000`, `AUTO_RUN_ID_PREFIX = "auto_"`, an `AUTO_MODE_REASONS` object mirroring `PIPELINE_REASONS`, and a client-side `resolveAutoModeConfig(settingsMap, projectId)` for the dialog. Add the server-side resolver in `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` as a direct copy of `resolveMaxConcurrentForProject` (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts:81`), re-read on every sweep so config changes apply without a restart. Because `PATCH /api/settings` always `JSON.stringify`s values (`app/api/settings/route.ts:71`), every parser must tolerate both raw and JSON-encoded forms — copy the `coerceNumber` body from `lib/night/constants.ts:81`.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` exists, imports nothing from `lib/db`, and is safely importable from a client component
- [ ] The five setting keys are exported with a global constant plus a `<key>:<projectId>` per-project override function
- [ ] `DEFAULT_AUTO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY = 2` and `DEFAULT_AUTO_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 1`; concurrency is clamped to 0..10 with 0 meaning "do not dispatch this kind"
- [ ] Every parser returns `null` for unconfigured/invalid input and accepts raw values, numeric strings, and JSON-encoded strings
- [ ] `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000` and `AUTO_RUN_ID_PREFIX = "auto_"` are exported; the prefix does not collide with `isNightRunId`'s `night_`
- [ ] `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` resolves per-project key → global key → built-in default, and is re-read on each call
- [ ] No database migration is added; `lib/db/migrations/` is untouched
- [ ] Unit tests cover the parser fall-through chain and the clamp boundaries

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want candidate selectors that identify buildable, reviewable and mergeable tickets, so that the supervisor never dispatches onto a ticket that is busy, waiting on a human, or already reviewed
user_stories.description: Create `lib/auto-mode/select.ts` with `selectBuildCandidates`, `selectReviewCandidates` and `selectMergeCandidates`. All three exclude tickets that have an active (`queued`/`running`) session via `getRunningSessionForTarget`, are owned by a live pipeline run (`pipelineRegistry`), DAG batch (`dagBatchRegistry`) or night run (`nightRunRegistry`) — the same three conflicts the batch route already refuses on (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/build/route.ts:742-775`) — are `isAwaitingReply`, or are parked. Build candidates follow the granularity rule: stories (status `todo` or `in_progress`) when the epic has stories, else the epic itself; skip anything whose epic is `done`/`released`; order by epic `priority DESC, position ASC` then story `position ASC`. Review candidates are epics in `review` passing the freshness guard. Merge candidates are epics in `review` with a non-null `branchName`, already reviewed since their last code change, and zero open `review_comments`. Use one batched query per sweep — follow `loadEpicStatuses` (`lib/dependencies/validation.ts:228`) and the LEFT-JOIN-IS-NULL idiom — never N per-ticket lookups. The module lives in `lib/auto-mode/` (not `lib/kanban/`, which is by convention client-safe and DB-free) but may import the pure `isAwaitingReply` predicate from it.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An epic in `review` whose newest terminal review session is newer than its newest terminal code session is NOT a review candidate (infinite re-review guard)
- [ ] An epic in `review` whose newest terminal session is a build IS a review candidate
- [ ] A ticket in `in_progress` whose latest session outcome is `asked_question` with no newer user comment is NOT a build candidate, and becomes one after the user comments
- [ ] A ticket with a `queued` or `running` session is excluded from all three selectors
- [ ] Tickets owned by a live pipeline run, DAG batch or night run are excluded from all three selectors
- [ ] An epic with user stories yields story-scoped build candidates; an epic without yields itself as an epic-scoped candidate
- [ ] An epic with at least one open `review_comment` is NOT a merge candidate
- [ ] Tickets whose epic is `done` or `released` are never candidates
- [ ] Each selector issues a bounded number of queries independent of ticket count (no N+1)
- [ ] `__tests__/auto-mode-select.test.ts` covers every bullet above using `createTestDb()

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want a standing sweep engine with independent build and review budgets, so that the board drains itself continuously without ever exceeding the concurrency I configured
user_stories.description: Create `lib/auto-mode/registry.ts` (globalThis-backed, modeled on `NightRunRegistry`: enabled flag, in-flight build and review session id sets, last sweep timestamp, rolling recent-dispatch list, and a parked map of `ticketId → consecutive failure count`) and `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts` (the sweep, guarded by a per-project mutex so two ticks never overlap). Sweep order: read config and bail if disabled; reconcile in-flight ids whose session rows are terminal; merge every merge candidate (cheap, no slot) to free the `review` column first; then dispatch reviews while `inFlightReviews < M`; then builds while `inFlightBuilds < N`. Every action is logged via `logTransition` (actor `system`, `"Auto mode "`-prefixed reason) so the ticket activity feed explains why an agent appeared unprompted. Dispatch reuses `createPipelineStageDriver({projectId, scope, epicId, userStoryId, buildNamedAgentId, reviewNamedAgentId, batchRunId: 'auto_<projectId>'}).launchStage({stage, attempt: 1, fixCycle: 0, previousAttemptSessionId: null, lastCodeSessionId: null})`, calling the driver's own `checkGuards(ownSessionIds)` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:205`) immediately before each dispatch as the last-moment race check. Three consecutive failures parks a ticket. Start/stop mirror the watchdog: idempotent `startAutoMode()`/`stopAutoMode()`, globalThis-backed `Symbol.for("arij.auto-mode")` interval, `.unref()`'d, with a pure `sweep(now)` exported for tests. Add `startAutoMode()` to `instrumentation.ts` next to `startSessionWatchdog()`, and chain an auto-mode kick into the session terminal hook — note `setSessionTerminalHook` is a single slot, so register one composed callback calling both `maybeAutoDistillAfterSessionTerminal` and the kick rather than overwriting it; the timer sweep stays as the backstop.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `startAutoMode()` is idempotent, survives dev hot reloads via a `globalThis` symbol, and its interval is `.unref()`'d so it never keeps the process alive
- [ ] A pure `sweep(now)` is exported and can be driven directly by tests with fake timers
- [ ] A per-project mutex guarantees two sweeps never overlap for the same project
- [ ] The engine never exceeds N in-flight builds or M in-flight reviews of its own dispatch
- [ ] Setting build or review concurrency to 0 disables that dispatch kind without disabling the other
- [ ] Dispatch goes through `createPipelineStageDriver(...).launchStage(...)` — not through HTTP routes, and not by duplicating the batch route's `launchEpic` closure
- [ ] Every dispatched session carries `batchRunId = auto_<projectId>` and is visible in the sessions viewer
- [ ] Every dispatch and skip writes a `logTransition` entry with actor `system` and an `"Auto mode "`-prefixed reason
- [ ] A ticket that fails 3 consecutive times is parked and skipped until the mode is toggled or the ticket is touched
- [ ] `instrumentation.ts` starts the mode and registers a composed terminal hook that preserves `maybeAutoDistillAfterSessionTerminal`
- [ ] Disabling the mode clears registry state and stops all further dispatch
- [ ] `__tests__/auto-mode-engine.test.ts` asserts the N/M caps, the mutex, and parking after 3 failures using an injected fake dispatcher and config resolver

user_stories.title: As a user, I want a clean review to merge the ticket automatically, so that finished work lands on main without me clicking Approve on every epic
user_stories.description: Create `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts` exposing `tryAutoMerge(projectId, epicId)`. Step 1: call `mergeWorktree(project.gitRepoPath, epic.branchName, worktreePath)` — plain git, no agent, no scheduler slot. Step 2 on success: call `applyTransition({fromStatus: 'review', toStatus: 'done', actor: 'agent', source: 'merge', reason: 'Auto mode: review clean, merged'})`, then update the epic to `status: 'done', branchName: null` and call `tryExportArjiJson(projectId)` — mirroring `merge/route.ts:77-102`. A guard refusal from `applyTransition` is logged and the epic is skipped, NOT parked, so it retries once its review comments are resolved. Step 3 on conflict: dispatch a merge-fix agent (`agentType: 'merge'`, prompt from `merge/route.ts:129-140`) counted against the build budget, then retry the merge once; a second failure parks the epic and raises a notification. The critical design constraint: the engine's `→ done` guards ARE the "review is OK" gate — `applyTransition` already refuses unless `hasCompletedReview` is true and `hasOpenReviewComments` is false (`lib/workflow/engine.ts:51-63`), so no new boolean is invented. `POST .../approve` must NOT be reused: it bulk-resolves every open review comment before transitioning (`approve/route.ts:30-38`), which would steamroll exactly the blocking findings that should stop an auto-merge.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A conflict-free merge runs as pure git: no agent session is created and no scheduler slot is consumed
- [ ] On success the epic moves to `done`, `branchName` is cleared, and `tryExportArjiJson` is called
- [ ] The transition goes through `applyTransition` with `source: 'merge'` so events and activity logs are emitted
- [ ] An epic with at least one open `review_comment` is never merged; the guard refusal is logged and the epic is skipped, not parked
- [ ] An epic with no completed review is never merged
- [ ] `POST .../approve` is not called anywhere in the auto-mode code path
- [ ] On merge conflict a merge-fix agent is dispatched, counted against the build budget, and the merge is retried once after it completes
- [ ] A second merge failure parks the epic and raises a notification instead of looping
- [ ] Integration test: an epic with a clean review merges end-to-end; the same epic with an open review comment does not

user_stories.title: As a user, I want to enable Full Auto Mode from the board and pick the build and review agents with their concurrency, so that I can start unattended work and see at a glance what it is doing
user_stories.description: Add `app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts` with GET returning `{ enabled, buildAgent, buildConcurrency, reviewAgent, reviewConcurrency, effectiveSchedulerBudget, inFlight: {build, review}, candidates: {build, review, merge}, parked[], recentDispatches[] }` and PUT writing the five settings keys and returning the new state — enabling triggers an immediate sweep instead of waiting for the next tick. Use `getProjectOr404` / `isErrorResponse` from `lib/api/route-helpers` like the night-run route. Build `components/auto-mode/AutoModeDialog.tsx` structured like `NightRunDialog.tsx`, reusing its `OptionRow` grammar, `NamedAgentSelect` (`components/shared/NamedAgentSelect.tsx`) and concurrency `Input`: an enable switch, then a build agent + build concurrency row and a review agent + review concurrency row, plus live candidate counts. Per the user's decision, when build + review concurrency exceeds the effective `agent_max_concurrent` budget the dialog shows a WARNING explaining that excess work will queue — it must never silently raise the scheduler budget. Mount the dialog beside the existing `NightRunDialog` in `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:795` with a toolbar toggle showing an active badge (`N building · M reviewing`) while the mode runs.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode` returns the full status shape including in-flight counts, candidate counts and parked tickets
- [ ] `PUT /api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode` persists the five settings keys and returns the new state
- [ ] Enabling the mode triggers an immediate sweep rather than waiting up to 15s
- [ ] Both routes 404 on an unknown project via `getProjectOr404`
- [ ] The dialog reuses `NamedAgentSelect` for both the build and the review agent
- [ ] Build and review concurrency are independently editable and clamped to 0..10
- [ ] When build + review concurrency exceeds `agent_max_concurrent`, a warning is displayed and the scheduler budget is NOT modified
- [ ] The toolbar toggle shows an active badge with live building/reviewing counts while the mode runs
- [ ] The chosen review agent is actually used by dispatched review sessions (not the default resolution)
- [ ] Component test asserts the warning appears exactly when N+M exceeds the effective budget

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want the pipeline stage driver to accept a review agent, so that the review agent chosen in Full Auto Mode is actually the one that runs
user_stories.description: PipelineStageDriverInit` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:118`) currently carries only `buildNamedAgentId`; the review stage resolves with `namedAgentId: null` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:306`) so that reviewer segregation can act. Add an optional `reviewNamedAgentId` field and pass it at line 306. The field must default to `null` so existing pipeline runs and night runs behave exactly as before — this is a purely additive change to a shared module used by the autonomous pipeline and the night engine, so regression coverage on those paths is the main risk to manage. When `reviewNamedAgentId` is null the existing `resolveAgentForDispatch(agentType, projectId, null, {purpose: 'review', ...})` behaviour with review-provider segregation is preserved unchanged.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `PipelineStageDriverInit` gains an optional `reviewNamedAgentId: string | null` field
- [ ] When set, the review stage resolves the named agent instead of passing `null`
- [ ] When null or omitted, resolution and review-provider segregation behave exactly as before the change
- [ ] Existing pipeline and night-run tests pass unchanged with no call-site edits required
- [ ] A test asserts a review stage dispatched with an explicit `reviewNamedAgentId` uses that agent's provider and model

user_stories.title: As a user, I want the supervisor to respect agent questions, in-flight runs and human actions, so that unattended mode never bulldozes work in progress or a question waiting for my answer
user_stories.description: End-to-end verification of the safety guards that make unattended operation trustworthy. Covers the four hazards identified during design: (1) infinite re-review — a passing review leaves the epic in `review`, so the freshness guard must ensure it is reviewed exactly once then merged; (2) bulldozing an agent's question — `handleAskedQuestionOutcome` (`lib/workflow/agent-question.ts:42`) holds the ticket in `in_progress`, indistinguishable from "returned from review", so `isAwaitingReply` must exclude it until the user replies; (3) coexistence — a night run, DAG batch or manual dispatch running concurrently must never result in two agents on one ticket, relying on `getRunningSessionForTarget` plus the three registry exclusions; (4) story serialization — the parent-epic guard (`lib/agents/concurrency.ts:65-70`) means stories of one epic run one at a time while many epics progress in parallel. Also verify restart behaviour: the mode resumes from settings on server boot and boot cleanup cancels orphaned `queued` sessions as usual. Document the mode in the README/docs including the merge-conflict behaviour, since that is the one path where an agent modifies main unattended.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Manual run: 3 epics in `todo` + 1 in `review` with build 2 / review 1 dispatches exactly 2 builders and 1 reviewer, with the third epic waiting
- [ ] Bounce loop: a negative review verdict returns the epic to `in_progress` and it is re-picked on the next sweep with no manual action
- [ ] Re-review guard: a passing review results in exactly one review session, followed by a merge
- [ ] Question guard: an `asked_question` outcome leaves the epic untouched in `in_progress`, and it is picked up only after a user comment
- [ ] Merge gate: an epic with one open review comment is not merged, and is merged on the next sweep after the comment is resolved
- [ ] Merge conflict: the merge-fix agent is dispatched, the retry runs, and a second failure parks the epic
- [ ] Story granularity: an epic with 3 stories builds them one at a time, flips to `review` when all are review/done, and is reviewed once at epic level
- [ ] Coexistence: starting a night run while Full Auto is on never results in two agents on one ticket
- [ ] Restart: the mode resumes from settings after a server restart and orphaned `queued` sessions are cancelled
- [ ] Documentation describes the mode, its settings keys, and explicitly calls out the unattended merge-conflict resolution behaviour

comments.content:
## Implémenté — commit `19eb33b`

Les 4 user stories sont livrées. Suite complète verte : **256 fichiers / 2475 tests**, `tsc --noEmit` OK, ESLint OK sur les fichiers touchés.

### US 1 — Sélecteur de source
`app/projects/import/page.tsx` : switch « Local folder » / « GitHub URL » (local par défaut), nouveau `components/import/GitHubUrlSelector.tsx` calqué sur `FolderSelector`. Bouton *Import* désactivé tant que la valeur ne parse pas, feedback inline sinon. Le changement de source vide l'erreur et le bloc debug.

### US 2 — Étapes distinctes
`ImportState` → `select | cloning | analyzing | preview`, `ImportProgress` prend un prop `step`. « Cloning owner/repo… » puis « Analyzing project… ». Clone réutilisé → note « Repository already cloned — updating. ». Échec de clone → retour à `select` dans la bannière destructive. Le parcours local va toujours directement à `analyzing`.

### US 3 — Projet déjà connecté
`handleValidate` transmet `githubOwnerRepo`, `gitRemoteUrl`, `cloneSource: "github"`, `defaultBranch`. `createProjectSchema` valide les trois nouveaux champs optionnels, `POST /api/projects` persiste `pathResult.normalizedPath` au lieu de l'entrée brute. `GitHubConnectBanner` reste masquée puisque `githubOwnerRepo` est déjà renseigné.

### US 4 — Échecs remontés
`projectData.data.id` n'est plus lu sans contrôle (une 400 levait avant) : la preview reste éditable avec le message de l'API. Chaque étape (clone, import, create, epics, stories, sync) a son propre message ; un epic en échec n'empêche pas les suivants ; un import partiel affiche toujours un lien vers le projet créé, et le bouton se verrouille pour éviter un doublon. `app/projects/new/page.tsx` rend `data.error`.

---

### Deux points à arbitrer à l'intégration

**1. `POST /api/projects/clone` n'existe pas encore sur `main`.** Il appartient à l'epic « Service de clone git », dont la branche est encore vide. L'UI est écrite contre le contrat documenté `{ path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }` et chaque branche est couverte par des tests à fetch mocké — mais le parcours n'est vérifiable de bout en bout (donc le critère « envoyer un epic en dev crée un worktree ») qu'une fois cet epic mergé.

**2. J'ai pris deux morceaux qui débordent du périmètre UI, faute de quoi l'epic n'était pas livrable :**

- **Migration `0027_project_clone_source.sql`** (`clone_source`, `git_remote_url`, `default_branch`), écrite à la main, journal `idx: 26`, `drizzle-kit generate` non lancé. Sans ces colonnes, le critère « le projet a `clone_source = "github"` » ne peut pas passer. J'ai aussi ajouté les entrées `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` et corrigé les deux simulations de base legacy dans `db-init.test.ts` — elles doivent supprimer les nouvelles colonnes, sinon la plus récente remonte le plafond de stamping au-dessus des ALTER 0023–0026 qu'elles testent. **Si un epic voisin livre aussi 0027, il faut dédupliquer.**

- **`lib/git/github-url.ts`**, module de parsing client-safe. La branche « Parsing et validation des URL GitHub » (commit `934f0d4`) place `parseGitHubRepoInput()` dans `lib/git/remote.ts`, qui importe `simple-git` au niveau module et ne peut donc pas atterrir dans un bundle navigateur — or le critère « bouton désactivé tant que la valeur ne parse pas » impose un parsing côté client. Même grammaire, mêmes rejets (`..`, `-` en tête, NUL, séparateurs). **À l'intégration, `remote.ts` devrait ré-exporter depuis `github-url.ts` plutôt que garder une seconde copie.**

Je n'ai volontairement pas touché à `lib/git/remote.ts`, `app/api/projects/clone/route.ts` ni au `/projects` du `.gitignore` (epic « socle du workspace ») pour éviter des conflits inutiles.

# Code Review Report

## 1. Readability

No issues found.

The import state machine and step-specific helper functions are clearly named and documented.

## 2. DRY Principle

No issues found.

## 3. Error Handling

### Finding 1

- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:460`
- **Description:** After partial project creation, `createdProjectId` is never cleared. Clicking Cancel clears `issues`, hides the partial-project link, and returns to selection; every subsequent preview remains permanently disabled because `busy` stays true. Cancel also remains enabled while validation is running, allowing the asynchronous chain to redirect or update state after the user leaves the preview.
- **Recommendation:** Represent partial creation as a dedicated state. Disable or redefine Cancel while creation runs, preserve access to the created project, and reset the ID only when deliberately starting a new import. Add a partial failure → Cancel → new import regression test.

## 4. Performance

No issues found.

The sequential epic/story creation matches the existing import pipeline and expected data volume.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found.

## 6. Type Safety

### Finding 2

- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:122`
- **Description:** `sendJson()` treats a successful HTTP response with invalid JSON or no `data` envelope as success through an unchecked cast. `runAnalysis()` subsequently dereferences `result.data.preview`, which can throw and leave the screen stuck on “Analyzing”.
- **Recommendation:** Treat missing or malformed response data as a failed request, preferably by validating endpoint-specific response shapes. Add coverage for a 2xx non-JSON or malformed response.

## 7. Testing and Functional Coverage

### Finding 3

- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:53`
- **Description:** The imported `default_branch` is stored but never used. `createWorktree()` still selects `main`, otherwise `master`. A freshly cloned repository whose default branch is `develop`, `trunk`, or another valid name will attempt to create its worktree from nonexistent `master`, violating the fresh-clone development acceptance criterion.
- **Recommendation:** Pass the stored default branch into worktree, merge, and release operations, verify that it exists, and fall back to the current branch or `origin/HEAD`. Add coverage for a repository with a non-`main`/`master` default branch.

## 8. API Design

### Finding 4

- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/route.ts:139`
- **Description:** `POST /api/projects` trusts the client-provided `cloneSource: "github"` ownership flag without proving the path was created by Arij or matches the supplied repository metadata. A crafted request can mark an arbitrary existing directory under the managed root as Arij-owned, making it eligible for later recursive clone cleanup. The route also accepts inconsistent or credential-bearing remote metadata.
- **Recommendation:** When `cloneSource` is present, require the complete metadata tuple, validate the clean GitHub URL and `owner/repo`, require the normalized path to equal the deterministic managed destination, and verify its origin. Reject inconsistent metadata.

### Finding 5

- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `lib/git/github-url.ts:54`
- **Description:** `segment.includes("..")` rejects names containing embedded consecutive dots, while the specification only rejects segments exactly equal to `.` or `..`. Embedded dots inside an already isolated path segment cannot perform directory traversal.
- **Recommendation:** Use exact `segment === "." || segment === ".."` checks and add a regression case such as `owner/repo..v2`.

## Validation

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: passed
- ESLint on touched source and test files: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- Clone endpoint response envelope was checked against its sibling implementation and matches the UI.
- Vitest could not start in this read-only sandbox because its workers could not create their temporary directory under `/tmp`; no test assertions ran during this review.
- Structured Arij submission was attempted, but the connector required approval while this session’s approval policy was `never`.

## Summary

- Critical: 0
- Major: 3
- Minor: 2
- Suggestions: 0

The source-switch and progress flows are well implemented, but the worktree default-branch failure, untrusted ownership metadata, and partial-import dead end are blocking.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

**Code Review**

# Code Review Report — "Parcours d'import depuis une URL GitHub (UI)"

Scope reviewed: `app/projects/import/page.tsx`, `app/projects/new/page.tsx`, `components/import/{FolderSelector,GitHubUrlSelector,ImportProgress,ImportPreview}.tsx`, `lib/git/github-url.ts`, `lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/validation/schemas.ts`, `app/api/projects/route.ts`, `app/api/projects/import/route.ts`, `lib/db/migrations/0027_project_clone_source.sql` + `meta/_journal.json`, `lib/db/init.ts`, and the six new/updated test files. Commits `19eb33b`, `249d9eb` on base `c9d404e`.

Overall the implementation is strong: the state machine is clean, the client-safe parser split is well justified, the migration/journal/legacy-baseline handling is correct (0027 at `idx: 26`, `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` entry, `db-init.test.ts` legacy simulations updated), and test coverage is direct for every story. The findings below are mostly about the failure paths this epic exists to harden — two of them are re-openings of findings from the previous review round that were not fully addressed.

## 1. Readability

No issues found.

Names are descriptive (`sendJson`, `applyProjectUpdate`, `createEpicsAndStories`, `exportArjiJson`, `resolveBaseBranch`), the non-obvious decisions carry good comments (why `cloneInfo`-gated metadata, why the preview is locked once a project row exists, why `main`/`master` keep priority), and the step helpers read top-to-bottom.

## 2. DRY Principle

### Finding 1
- **Severity:** Suggestion
- **Location:** `lib/git/github-url.ts:13-21` vs `lib/git/remote.ts:40-45`
- **Description:** The four remote-URL regexes are duplicated between the new client-safe module and the existing `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`. The module doc says `remote.ts` should re-export at integration, but nothing enforces it and `remote.ts` on this branch has no `parseGitHubRepoInput` at all — so today there is *no* shared source of truth, and the two grammars can drift (they already differ on segment safety: `remote.ts` performs no `.`/`..`/leading-`-` checks).
- **Recommendation:** At integration, make `github-url.ts` the single grammar owner and have `remote.ts` re-export/compose from it; add a parity test asserting both modules reject the same inputs.

### Finding 2
- **Severity:** Suggestion
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:36` and `components/import/ImportPreview.tsx:11`
- **Description:** `ImportData` is declared twice with subtly different fields (the page's copy adds `status`, `spec`, `priority`, `position`; the preview's doesn't). Structural typing papers over the divergence, but a new arji.json field now has to be added in two places.
- **Recommendation:** Hoist one `ImportData` type to a shared module (e.g. `lib/sync/arji-json.ts` or a `components/import/types.ts`) and import it in both.

## 3. Error Handling

### Finding 3
- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:122` (unchecked cast) and `app/projects/import/page.tsx:246` (unguarded dereference)
- **Description:** `sendJson()` still treats a 2xx response with a malformed or envelope-less body as success: `response.json().catch(() => null)` yields `null`/`{}`/a scalar, and the function returns `{ ok: true, data: payload?.data as T }` — i.e. `data === undefined` — without any check. `runAnalysis()` then does `setImportData(result.data.preview)`, which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. There is no try/catch around `runAnalysis` in either `handleAnalyze` or `handleGitHubImport`, so the rejection is unhandled and the state is never left `"analyzing"`. Result: a permanent "Analyzing project…" spinner with no error and no recovery except reload. This is exactly the previous review's Finding 2, still open, on the epic's primary flow — and it defeats US4's "never left on a dead screen" goal.
- **Recommendation:** Treat `payload === null` / non-object payload / missing expected envelope as a failed request (`ok: false`, error like "unexpected response from /api/projects/import"), and/or validate endpoint-specific shapes. Add a test: 2xx with non-JSON body and 2xx with `{}` for `/api/projects/import` must land back on `select` with the message rendered.

### Finding 4
- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:311` (only write of `createdProjectId`, never reset), `:460` (`busy={validating || createdProjectId !== null}`), `:462-464` (Cancel handler)
- **Description:** The partial-creation dead end from the previous review's Finding 1 was only half-fixed. Sequence: GitHub import → project created → one epic fails → issues + "Open the partially created project" link shown, Validate disabled. User clicks **Cancel** → `resetFeedback()` clears the issues and link, state → `select`, but `createdProjectId` survives. The user starts another import (natural action), spends minutes on clone + analysis, and lands on a preview where "Validate & Import" is **permanently disabled with no message and no link** — a dead screen reachable through the epic's own happy-path failure. Additionally, Cancel remains clickable while `validating` is true: the in-flight chain keeps running after the user left the preview, so a late `router.push` or a late `setIssues`/`setError` can land on top of a *second, concurrent* import flow (stale `cloneInfo`/`folderPath` interleaving included).
- **Recommendation:** (a) Disable (or no-op) Cancel while `validating`; (b) reset `createdProjectId` when the user deliberately starts a new import (`handleAnalyze`/`handleGitHubImport`), which also un-locks the preview. Add the regression test the previous review asked for: partial failure → Cancel → new import → Validate must be enabled.

### Finding 5
- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:18-27` (`DebugInfo`) and the debug `<details>` block; producer side `app/api/projects/import/route.ts` (`debug: { stack }`, `{ duration, rawPreview }`, `{ duration, keys }`)
- **Description:** The debug contract is partially lost in transit: `stack` is declared on `DebugInfo` but never rendered, and the import route's `rawPreview` / `keys` fields are not in the type at all. For the `{ stack }` debug shape (unexpected server error) the "Debug info" disclosure renders an empty body; for invalid-arji.json failures the most useful field (`rawPreview`) is silently dropped. This undercuts the "every step reports its own failure" goal for the two most diagnostic cases.
- **Recommendation:** Render `stack`, and add `rawPreview`/`keys` to `DebugInfo` (or a generic `Record<string, unknown>` escape hatch) plus one test each.

Positive: everything else in the chain is handled — clone failure returns to `select` with a context-prefixed message, a clone response missing `path` is caught, create-failure keeps the preview editable with the API message + zod `details` expansion, each epic/story/sync/patch step reports distinctly, a failed epic skips its stories without orphans and continues, and `new/page.tsx` now surfaces `data.error` with a status-code fallback and network-failure path.

## 4. Performance

No issues found.

Sequential epic/story creation matches the existing pipeline and the data volumes involved (dozens of tickets). `parseGitHubRepoInput` per keystroke is a handful of regexes. `structuredClone` on edit per keystroke in `ImportPreview` is pre-existing and negligible at preview size. No re-render hazards: `ImportProgress`/selectors are trivial, the page is conditionally rendered per state.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found.

`camelCase` throughout, components in PascalCase, `ImportSource`/`ImportState`/`CloneInfo`/`GitHubImportRequest` all read well; `app/projects/import/page.tsx` copy uses consistent "…" ellipsis vs "..." only in the progress headings (`"Cloning Orolol/arij..."`) — cosmetic at most, not worth a change.

## 6. Type Safety

### Finding 6
- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `lib/git/github-url.ts:46`
- **Description:** `isSafeRepoSegment` rejects any segment *containing* `..` (`segment.includes("..")`), but the spec (and the previous review's Finding 5) only rejects segments exactly equal to `.` or `..`. GitHub repo names may contain consecutive dots, so `owner/repo..v2` (a valid, creatable repo) is rejected by the button, by the parse, and — via the same grammar — by any server re-parse. The over-rejection is safe (no traversal risk inside an already-isolated segment) but silently makes valid repos un-importable.
- **Recommendation:** Use exact `segment === "." || segment === ".."` and add a `owner/repo..v2` acceptance regression case.

No `any` types anywhere in the touched code. The one unchecked cast is `payload?.data as T` at `page.tsx:122` — already covered by Finding 3.

## 7. Testing

Coverage is the epic's strongest asset: `github-url-client-parser.test.ts` (accept/reject matrix, suffix stripping, no-simple-git-leak check), `github-url-selector.test.tsx` (11), `import-page-github-flow.test.tsx` (18, including gated-response sequencing for the clone→analyze→preview transitions), `import-progress-step.test.tsx` (4), `new-project-page-errors.test.tsx` (4), `projects-create-clone-metadata.test.ts` (9), three new `createWorktree` cases for the `origin/HEAD` path, and the `db-init.test.ts` legacy simulations updated for 0027.

### Finding 7
- **Severity:** Suggestion
- **Location:** `__tests__/import-page-github-flow.test.tsx`, `__tests__/worktree-manager.test.ts`, `__tests__/github-url-client-parser.test.ts`
- **Description:** The suite is comprehensive on the happy path and on per-step failures, but each of the findings above sits exactly in an untested seam: no 2xx envelope-less response case (Finding 3), no "partial import → Cancel → new import" case (Finding 4), no `mergeWorktree` with a non-main/master default (Finding 8), no embedded-`..` parse case (Finding 6).
- **Recommendation:** Add those four regression tests; the fetch-mock harness in `import-page-github-flow.test.tsx` already supports all of them.

## 8. API Design

### Finding 8
- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:124` (`const mainBranch = branches.all.includes("main") ? "main" : "master";`), consumed by `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/merge/route.ts:75,210` and `resolve-merge/route.ts:98,245`
- **Description:** The `249d9eb` fix threaded real-default-branch resolution through `createWorktree` (via `resolveBaseBranch` → `origin/HEAD`) and `release.ts`'s `pickBaseBranch` already falls back to `branches[0]` — but `mergeWorktree` still hard-guesses `main`/`master` and then `git.checkout(mainBranch)`. On a freshly cloned repo whose default is `develop`/`trunk` (the exact class this epic exists to support), the epic can now be built (thanks to the fix) but **cannot be merged back**: checkout of non-existent `master` fails, so the review→merge loop — Arij's core lifecycle — breaks with a confusing error. Before this epic such repos couldn't even reach that point (worktree creation failed first), so the fix newly exposes the gap; spec §4.5 states `default_branch` is used "instead of the main/master guess", and the migration header itself says the code should "stop guessing between main and master".
- **Recommendation:** Extract the resolution (local `main` → local `master` → `origin/HEAD` → current branch) into a shared helper and use it in `mergeWorktree` as the merge target, or thread `projects.default_branch` from the row through the merge routes. Add a `develop`-default repo test for the merge path.

### Finding 9
- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/route.ts:109-142`
- **Description:** `POST /api/projects` accepts the client-asserted `cloneSource: "github"` ownership flag (plus `gitRemoteUrl`/`defaultBranch`) with no consistency check: nothing verifies `githubOwnerRepo` matches `gitRemoteUrl`, that the remote parses as GitHub, that `gitRepoPath` lies under the managed clone root, or that the directory's actual `origin` matches. A crafted request can mark any existing directory as Arij-owned. No deletion consumer exists on this branch yet (the `DELETE` route only removes the row), so this is latent — but the write side ships now and the destructive cleanup consumer is the sibling epic's next step, which makes the flag a data-loss flag in waiting.
- **Recommendation:** When `cloneSource` is present, require the full metadata tuple, validate the clean GitHub URL + `owner/repo` with the existing parser, require the normalized path under the managed root, and (ideally) verify the directory's `origin`. At minimum, block this before the clone-cleanup epic lands.

Positive on API design otherwise: splitting clone from analysis was the right call; the UI sends the *raw pasted value* to the clone endpoint and lets the server re-parse authoritatively (the client parse is display/disabling only); statuses are correct (400 validation, 201 create); response envelopes are consistent `{ data }` / `{ error, details }`; and `POST /api/projects` now persisting `pathResult.normalizedPath` is a genuine improvement the tests pin down.

## Integration risks (cross-epic, not defects on this branch)

1. **`POST /api/projects/clone` does not exist on this branch** (sibling "clone service" epic). The UI is written against the documented `{ path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }` contract with mocked-fetch coverage of every branch — verify the contract verbatim at merge, including the 409 mismatch-remote case the UI surfaces.
2. **`/projects` is still absent from `.gitignore`** (spec §4.1). Explicitly deferred to the workspace-layout epic — confirm it lands there, or dogfooding shows every clone as untracked.
3. **Migration `0027` dedupe risk** — if a sibling epic also ships `0027_project_clone_source`, the journal entry and the `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` rows must be merged, not duplicated.
4. **`remote.ts` re-export** — see Finding 1.

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 3 (Findings 3, 4, 8) |
| Minor | 3 (Findings 5, 6, 9) |
| Suggestion | 3 (Findings 1, 2, 7) |

The UI itself — source switch, distinct progress steps, clone-metadata forwarding, per-step failure surfacing, and the `origin/HEAD` worktree fix — is well built and well tested. But the failure-path hardening that US4 promises has two real dead ends still in it (the 2xx envelope-less freeze and the post-Cancel permanently-locked preview), and the worktree fix's newly-reachable merge path still hard-guesses `main`/`master`, breaking the lifecycle for the exact class of repos this feature imports.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: Kanban Workflow Stability & Real-Time Synchronization
epics.description:
Comprehensive refactor of the ticket workflow system to eliminate erratic behaviors, ensure consistent state transitions, and provide real-time updates without page refresh. This epic addresses critical bugs where tickets move to 'Done' prematurely or don't respect review workflows, while adding WebSocket-based live synchronization and enhanced visual feedback through animations.

Implementation Plan:
1. Workflow Rule Engine: Implement strict state machine for ticket transitions with explicit guards (e.g., no 'Done' without completed review, no premature closure when agent asks questions)
2. WebSocket Infrastructure: Set up Socket.io or native WebSocket server for bidirectional communication, broadcasting ticket updates, agent session status, and column movements to all connected clients
3. Event-Driven Architecture: Unify agent hooks (build complete, review complete) and manual user actions under consistent event bus that enforces workflow rules
4. Animation System: Enhance dnd-kit with custom transitions for programmatic moves (agent-triggered) and add visual indicators (sounds optional, glow effects) for state changes
5. Optimistic UI Updates: Implement optimistic updates with rollback capability for instant feedback, confirmed by WebSocket events
6. Agent Session Integration: Ensure agent session lifecycle (start, resume, completion) properly gates ticket transitions and broadcasts status in real-time
